Polity.keywords: Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha, Speaker, Anti-Defection (10th Schedule), Question Hour

sub_items.text: Composition of Rajya Sabha (Max 250, 12 nominated by President Art 80) & Lok Sabha (Art 81)
Qualifications & Disqualifications: Office of profit (Art 102), Unsound mind, Undischarged insolvent
Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule, 52nd & 91st Amendments): Speaker's decision subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan 1992)
Presiding Officers: Speaker election, resignation to Dy Speaker, casting vote only on equality (Art 100)
Sessions: Summoning, Prorogation (by President) vs Adjournment sine die (by Presiding Officer), Dissolution
Business Conduct: Question Hour (Starred/Unstarred/Short Notice) vs Zero Hour (Indian innovation since 1962, not in rules)

Polity.topic: Parliament: Legislative & Financial Procedures (Money Bills, Budget)
Polity.keywords: Art 110, Art 108 Joint Sitting, Cut Motions, PAC, Estimates Committee

sub_items.text: Money Bill (Art 110): Certified exclusively by Speaker, Rajya Sabha cannot amend/reject, 14 days time limit, no joint sitting
Financial Bills: Art 117(1) vs Art 117(3) differences in introduction and voting
Joint Sitting (Art 108): Summoned by President, presided by Speaker, simple majority, NOT available for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills
Budget Process: Annual Financial Statement (Art 112), Demand for Grants (LS only), Appropriation Bill (Art 114), Finance Bill
Cut Motions: Disapproval of Policy Cut (to ₹1), Economy Cut, Token Cut (by ₹100)
Parliamentary Committees: PAC (22 members: 15 LS + 7 RS, Minister cannot be member), Estimates Committee (30 members, LS only)

Polity.topic: Union & State Executive: President vs Governor Powers
Polity.keywords: Art 72 vs 161 (Pardoning), Art 123 vs 213 (Ordinance), Discretion, Assent to Bills Art 200

sub_items.text: Presidential Election (Art 54 & 55): Elected members of LS, RS, and State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi & Puducherry); proportional representation with single transferable vote
Presidential Impeachment (Art 61): Quasi-judicial procedure; NOMINATED members of Parliament participate; State Assemblies DO NOT participate
Pardoning Powers (Art 72 vs Art 161): President can pardon death sentences and court-martial; Governor CANNOT pardon death sentences
Ordinance Making (Art 123 for President, Art 213 for Governor): Must be approved within 6 weeks of reassembly; cannot override Fundamental Rights
Discretionary Powers: Governor has constitutional discretion (Art 163) while President only has situational discretion
Council of Ministers (Art 74 & 75): Collective responsibility to Lok Sabha; total ministers cannot exceed 15% of LS strength (91st Amendment)

Polity.keywords: Reasonable restrictions, Right to Privacy (Puttaswamy), Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Quo-Warranto

sub_items.text: Article 14 & 15: Equality before law (British) vs Equal protection of laws (US); Prohibition of discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth
Article 19: 6 freedoms with reasonable restrictions; doctrine of proportionality (Puttaswamy judgement)
Article 20 & 21: Protection against ex-post facto laws, double jeopardy, self-incrimination; Right to Life & Personal Liberty; cannot be suspended during National Emergency (44th Amendment)
Article 25–28: Freedom of religion, individual vs denominational rights; subject to public order, morality, and health
Article 32 & 226: Writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus (not against President/Governor), Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari; SC jurisdiction narrower than HC
Judicial Review & Non-citizens: FRs available to citizens ONLY: Art 15, 16, 19, 29, 30; FRs available to foreigners also: Art 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25-28

Polity.topic: Judiciary: Supreme Court & High Courts Jurisdiction
Polity.keywords: Original Jurisdiction, Judicial Review, Curative Petition, Collegium system, Contempt

sub_items.text: Supreme Court Composition & Collegium System: CJI + 4 senior-most judges for SC appointments; 3 Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998) & NJAC strike-down (99th Amendment)
Jurisdiction of Supreme Court: Original (Art 131 - federal disputes exclusively), Appellate (Art 132-134), Advisory (Art 143 - President reference)
Special Leave Petition (Art 136): Discretionary appellate power over any court/tribunal except military tribunals
Complete Justice (Art 142): Inherent power to pass decree or order for doing complete justice
High Courts: Power of superintendence (Art 227); Transfer of judges; Writ jurisdiction (Art 226 wider than Art 32 as it covers ordinary legal rights)
Subordinate Judiciary: Appointment of District Judges by Governor in consultation with High Court (Art 233)

Polity.topic: Constitutional Bodies: ECI, CAG, Finance Commission, UPSC
Polity.keywords: Art 324, Art 148, Art 280, Removal process, Constitutional safeguards

sub_items.text: Election Commission of India (Art 324): Appointment process (CJI, PM, LoP panel reforms), removal of CEC same as SC Judge; Election Commissioners removed on CEC recommendation
Comptroller & Auditor General (Art 148–151): Guardian of public purse; audited reports submitted to President $\rightarrow$ examined by Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
Finance Commission (Art 280): Quinquennial body; 1 Chairman + 4 members; recommend vertical devolution (Centre to States) and horizontal distribution formulas
UPSC & State PSCs (Art 315–323): Advisory functions; members removed by President on reference to Supreme Court under Art 317
National Commission for SCs (Art 338), STs (Art 338A), and BCs (Art 338B - added by 102nd Amendment): Civil court inquiry powers
Attorney General (Art 76): Appointed by President; right of audience in all courts, right to speak in Parliament without right to vote

Polity.keywords: Compulsory vs Voluntary provisions, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission, PESA Act 1996

sub_items.text: 73rd Amendment (1992) - Part IX & 11th Schedule: 29 functional items; 3-tier system (Gram, Intermediate, District)

Compulsory Provisions: Gram Sabha (Art 243A), 5-year fixed tenure, direct elections to all seats, 1/3rd reservation for women, State Finance Commission (Art 243I), State Election Commission (Art 243K)
Voluntary Provisions: Devolution of 29 subjects, reservation for OBCs, voting rights to MLAs/MPs in panchayats
PESA Act 1996 (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas): Extends Part IX to 5th Schedule areas; empowers Gram Sabha over minor forest produce, land alienation, dispute resolution
74th Amendment (1992) - Part IXA & 12th Schedule: 18 functional items; Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, Municipal Corporations; Ward Committees
District Planning Committee (Art 243ZD) & Metropolitan Planning Committee (Art 243ZE): Consolidates rural & urban plans

Polity.topic: Directive Principles of State Policy & Fundamental Duties
Polity.keywords: Socialistic, Gandhian, Liberal-intellectual, Art 39(b) & (c), 42nd Amendment additions

sub_items.text: DPSPs (Part IV, Art 36–51): Borrowed from Irish Constitution; non-justiciable (Art 37) but fundamental in the governance of the country
Classification: Socialistic (Art 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A), Gandhian (Art 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47, 48), Liberal-Intellectual (Art 44 Uniform Civil Code, 45, 48A, 49, 50, 51)
42nd Amendment Additions: Art 39(f) (healthy development of children), Art 39A (equal justice & free legal aid), Art 43A (workers' participation), Art 48A (environment protection)
44th Amendment Addition: Art 38(2) (minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities)
Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Art 51A): Added by 42nd Amendment on Swaran Singh Committee recommendation (10 duties); 11th duty added by 86th Amendment (education for 6-14 age)
Enforceability: Verma Committee (1999) identified existing legal provisions enforcing FDs (Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, WPA 1972, RPA 1951)

Polity.keywords: 7th Schedule (Union, State, Concurrent), Art 352, Art 356, Inter-State Council Art 263

sub_items.text: Legislative Relations (Art 245–255): 7th Schedule Lists; Union List (exclusive), State List, Concurrent List; Residuary powers with Parliament (Art 248)
Parliament legislating on State subjects: Under Art 249 (RS resolution by 2/3rd present & voting), Art 250 (National Emergency), Art 252 (2 or more states agree), Art 253 (International treaties)

Administrative Relations (Art 256–263): Inter-State Council (Art 263 - set up by President on Sarkaria Commission advice), Inter-State River Water Disputes (Art 262 - Parliament can bar SC jurisdiction)
Financial Relations (Art 268–293): GST Council (Art 279A - 1/3rd Centre voting, 2/3rd States voting, 3/4th majority needed for decisions)
National Emergency (Art 352): Grounds: War, external aggression, or 'armed rebellion' (substituted for internal disturbance by 44th Amend); Parliamentary approval within 1 month by special majority
President's Rule (Art 356 & 365): Failure of constitutional machinery; S.R. Bommai case (1994) guidelines - floor test mandatory, court can revive dissolved assembly

Polity.keywords: Disqualification on conviction, Model Code of Conduct, Delimitation Commission, EVM-VVPAT

sub_items.text: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951: RPA 1950 covers voter qualifications, delimitation of constituencies, electoral rolls; RPA 1951 covers conduct of elections, qualifications/disqualifications of candidates, corrupt practices
Disqualification under RPA 1951 (Sec 8): Conviction for specified offenses or imprisonment for $\ge$ 2 years; Lily Thomas judgement (2013) struck down Sec 8(4) instant stay
Electoral Reforms: NOTA introduced post-PUCL case 2013; VVPAT mandatory verification post-2019; Electoral Bonds scheme struck down in Association for Democratic Reforms (2024)
Model Code of Conduct (MCC): Non-statutory operational guidelines; comes into force immediately upon election announcement
Delimitation Commission: Appointed by President; orders have force of law and CANNOT be questioned in any court; based on census (currently frozen till post-2026)
Simultaneous Elections (One Nation One Election): Kovind Committee recommendations, constitutional amendments needed (Art 83, 85, 172, 174, 356)

Polity.keywords: Kesavananda Bharati, Art 368 types of majority, 9th Schedule judicial review

sub_items.text: Amendment Procedure (Art 368): Simple majority (outside Art 368), Special majority (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present & voting), Special majority + ratification by 50% state legislatures
Federal Provisions requiring State Ratification: Election of President, executive powers of Union/State, Supreme Court & High Courts, 7th Schedule lists, representation in Parliament, Art 368 itself
Basic Structure Doctrine: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973 - 13 judge bench); includes supremacy of Constitution, secularism, federalism, judicial review, separation of powers, free & fair elections
Landmark Cases: Shankari Prasad (1951) $\rightarrow$ Golaknath (1967) $\rightarrow$ Kesavananda (1973) $\rightarrow$ Indira Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975) $\rightarrow$ Minerva Mills (1980)

Key Amendments: 42nd (Mini-Constitution), 44th (Restoration of rights), 52nd (Anti-defection), 61st (Voting age 21 to 18), 73rd/74th (Local governance), 86th (RTE Art 21A), 91st (Ministry 15% cap), 101st (GST), 103rd (EWS 10%), 106th (Nari Shakti Vandan - 33% women quota)

Polity.keywords: CAA provisions, 5th Schedule vs 6th Schedule Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)

sub_items.text: Citizenship (Part II, Art 5–11 & Citizenship Act 1955): Acquisition by Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, Incorporation of territory; Single citizenship principle
Loss of Citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, Deprivation; OCI cardholders (no political rights, cannot buy agricultural land, no constitutional post)
5th Schedule (Art 244(1)): Applies to scheduled areas in 10 states (excluding 6th Schedule states); Governor has legislative power to adapt laws; Tribes Advisory Council (TAC)
6th Schedule (Art 244(2)): Applies exclusively to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (AMTM); Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) with legislative, executive and judicial powers
Official Language (Part XVII, Art 343–351): Hindi in Devanagari script is official language of Union; English continued as associate; 8th Schedule (22 languages; English is NOT included)

Economy.topic: Monetary Policy Framework & RBI Policy Tools
Economy.keywords: Repo, SDF, MSF, CRR, SLR, OMO, Monetary Policy Committee (MPC composition & voting)

sub_items.text: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): 6 members (3 RBI + 3 GoI appointed); chaired by RBI Governor with casting vote; 4% (+/- 2%) CPI inflation targeting mandate

Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF): Repo Rate (RBI lends against collateral), Reverse Repo Rate, Standing Deposit Facility (SDF - absorbs liquidity without collateral), Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)
Statutory Reserve Ratios: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR - cash kept with RBI, no interest earned) vs Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR - liquid assets like G-Secs, cash, gold kept with bank itself)
Open Market Operations (OMOs): Outright purchase/sale of G-Secs to inject/absorb durable liquidity; Operation Twist (simultaneous buy long-term & sell short-term G-Secs)
Transmission Mechanism: Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) $\rightarrow$ External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR linked to Repo/T-bill)
Money Supply Aggregates: Reserve Money (M0), Narrow Money (M1 = Currency + Demand Deposits + Other deposits with RBI), Broad Money (M3 = M1 + Time Deposits with banks); Money Multiplier = M3 / M0

Economy.topic: Banking Sector, NPA Resolution & Financial Inclusion
Economy.keywords: IBC (Insolvency Code), Bad Bank (NARCL), PCA framework, Basel III CRAR, Priority Sector Lending

sub_items.text: Capital Adequacy & Basel III Norms: Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR); Tier 1 Capital (Common Equity Core) vs Tier 2 Capital (Subordinated debt)

Asset Classification: Standard $\rightarrow$ Sub-standard ($\le$ 12 months) $\rightarrow$ Doubtful (> 12 months) $\rightarrow$ Loss Assets; Special Mention Accounts (SMA-0: 1-30 days, SMA-1: 31-60 days, SMA-2: 61-90 days)
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC 2016): National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for corporates; Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) timeline 180+90 days; Committee of Creditors (CoC)
Bad Bank Architecture: National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL - buys bad loans with 85% Security Receipts) + India Debt Resolution Co Ltd (IDRCL - sells assets)

Priority Sector Lending (PSL): 40% of ANBC for domestic scheduled commercial banks; 75% for Small Finance Banks & Payments Banks; Sub-targets for Agriculture (18%), Small & Marginal Farmers, Micro Enterprises
Differentiated Banks: Payments Banks (deposits up to ₹2 lakh, NO lending/credit cards) vs Small Finance Banks (basic banking, 75% PSL target, can lend)

Economy.keywords: MSP calculation (A2+FL, C2), CACP, Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS), PM-KISAN, e-NAM, FCI procurement

sub_items.text: Minimum Support Price (MSP): Announced by CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices) for 22 mandated crops + Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) for Sugarcane

Cost Calculation Formulas: A2 (paid-out costs) $\rightarrow$ A2+FL (paid-out costs + imputed unpaid family labour) $\rightarrow$ C2 (comprehensive cost including rent on land and interest on capital); Swaminathan Commission recommended 50% above C2; Govt announces MSP based on 1.5x A2+FL
Procurement & Buffer Stocks: Food Corporation of India (FCI) open-ended procurement; Operational stocks + Strategic reserve guidelines under PMGKAY / NFSA 2013

Subsidies Regime: Food Subsidy (Economic Cost of wheat/rice minus Central Issue Price), Fertilizer Subsidy (Nutrient Based Subsidy - NBS for P&K; Urea under direct price control), Power & Irrigation Subsidies

WTO Boxes on Agriculture: Green Box (non-trade distorting, research, decoupled payments, no limit), Blue Box (production-limiting subsidies), Amber Box (trade distorting, subject to de minimis 10% for developing nations); Peace Clause (Bali package)
Agricultural Marketing Reforms: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market pan-India electronic trading portal), Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Model APMC acts

Economy.topic: External Sector: Balance of Payments, Forex & Exchange Rates
Economy.keywords: Current Account Deficit (CAD), Capital Account, FDI vs FPI rules, NEER/REER, Devaluation impact

sub_items.text: Balance of Payments (BoP): Current Account (Trade balance of goods + Invisibles: services, remittances, transfers, income) vs Capital Account (FDI, FPI, External Commercial Borrowings, NRI deposits, banking capital)
Current Account Deficit (CAD) vs Fiscal Deficit: Twin deficit hypothesis; CAD financed by capital flows
FDI vs FPI: FDI (>10% equity stake, strategic, long-term, managerial control) vs FPI (<10% equity, liquid, hot money portfolio flows)
Rupee Convertibility: Current Account is FULLY convertible (since 1994, Art VIII IMF); Capital Account is PARTIALLY convertible (Tarapore Committee roadmaps)

Exchange Rate Dynamics: NEER (Nominal Effective Exchange Rate - trade-weighted basket of currencies) vs REER (Real Effective Exchange Rate = NEER adjusted for relative inflation differentials); REER > 100 indicates currency overvaluation
Forex Reserves: Components: Foreign Currency Assets (FCA), Gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs in IMF), Reserve Tranche Position (RTP in IMF)

Economy.keywords: Revenue vs Capital Expenditure, Fiscal Deficit, Primary Deficit, FRBM targets, Off-budget borrowing

sub_items.text: Government Receipts: Revenue Receipts (Tax revenue: Direct income/corporate tax + Indirect GST/customs; Non-tax revenue: dividends, interest, spectrum fees) vs Capital Receipts (Debt-creating: market borrowings; Non-debt: loan recovery, disinvestment)

Government Expenditure: Revenue Expenditure (operational, salaries, pensions, interest payments, subsidies) vs Capital Expenditure (infrastructure assets creation, roads, machinery, loans given to states)

Deficit Metrics: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure minus (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts); Revenue Deficit = Revenue Exp minus Revenue Receipts; Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments

FRBM Act 2003 & NK Singh Committee (2017): Targets: Debt-to-GDP ratio (60% combined: 40% Centre + 20% States), Fiscal Deficit glide path to 3% of GDP; Escape clauses (war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture, structural reforms)
Tax Reforms: Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas; Goods and Services Tax (GST) destination-based consumption tax; Input Tax Credit (ITC) mechanism and anti-profiteering
Treasury Management: Ways and Means Advances (WMA) temporary RBI overdraft to bridge revenue mismatches (Normal WMA + Special/Overdraft)

Economy.keywords: Bond Yields vs Price inverse curve, Treasury Bills (91/182/364 days), Sovereign Green Bonds, Commercial Paper

sub_items.text: Government Securities (G-Secs): Treasury Bills (T-Bills issued at discount, 91-day, 182-day, 364-day, NO interest coupon), Dated Securities (long-term, fixed/floating coupon, up to 40 years)
Bond Yields & Price Dynamics: Bond Price and Bond Yield move in OPPOSITE directions ($Yield = Coupon / Price$); Inverted Yield Curve signals recession fears
Sovereign Green Bonds: Funds earmarked for public sector renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation; lower borrowing yield (greenium)

Capital Market Instruments: Commercial Paper (unsecured short-term promissory note, corporates), Certificate of Deposit (issued by banks), Masala Bonds (rupee-denominated overseas bonds - currency risk with buyer)
SEBI Regulations: Primary Market (IPO, FPO, Rights Issue) vs Secondary Market (Stock Exchanges, T+1 settlement); Alternative Investment Funds (AIF Category I, II, III)
Municipal Bonds & Blue Bonds: Local body financing for urban infrastructure (AMRUT), oceanic conservation bonds

Economy.topic: Inflation Dynamics: CPI vs WPI & Price Indices
Economy.keywords: CPI-Combined (weights: food 45.8%), WPI (manufacturing goods), Headline vs Core inflation, GDP Deflator

sub_items.text: CPI vs WPI: Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined base 2012, CSO/NSO under MoSPI, covers goods + services, weighted high on Food & Beverages 45.86%, Headline inflation metric for RBI MPC) vs Wholesale Price Index (WPI base 2011-12, Office of Economic Adviser under DPIIT, covers goods ONLY, weighted high on Manufactured products 64.2%)
Core Inflation vs Headline Inflation: Headline includes volatile components (food & energy); Core Inflation = Headline minus (Food + Fuel/Energy)

Types of Inflation: Demand-Pull (excess aggregate demand, cheap credit) vs Cost-Push (supply bottlenecks, crude shock, crop failure); Stagflation (stagnant growth + high inflation + high unemployment)
Producer Price Index (PPI): Measures average change in prices received by domestic producers for their output, excludes trade and transport margins (working group recommendations)
Base Effect: The distorting impact of abnormally high or low price levels in the corresponding previous year on current inflation calculation

Index of Industrial Production (IIP): Base 2011-12, MoSPI, covers Mining, Manufacturing, Electricity; Eight Core Industries account for 40.27% of IIP (Refinery products > Electricity > Steel > Coal > Crude Oil > Natural Gas > Cement > Fertilizers)

Economy.topic: International Economic Organizations: WTO, IMF, World Bank
Economy.keywords: WTO Subsidies (Amber, Blue, Green boxes), TRIPS, IMF SDR basket, Article IV consultation

sub_items.text: World Trade Organization (WTO): Marrakesh Agreement 1994, consensus decision-making; Dispute Settlement Body (Appellate Body currently paralyzed due to US judge veto); Most Favoured Nation (MFN) & National Treatment principles
WTO Agreements: Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), TRIPS (patents, compulsory licensing, evergreen patents Sec 3(d) Indian Patent Act), TRIMS, GATS (services modes 1-4)

International Monetary Fund (IMF): Quota system determining voting power (SDR currency basket: USD, Euro, CNY, JPY, GBP); Extended Fund Facility (EFF), Rapid Financing Instrument, Article IV consultations
World Bank Group: IBRD (middle-income govts), IDA (poorest nations concessional loans), IFC (private sector arm), MIGA (political risk insurance), ICSID (dispute settlement - India is NOT a member)
Multilateral Development Banks: New Development Bank (NDB - BRICS bank, equal voting shares), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB - China largest shareholder, India 2nd largest shareholder)
Trade Blocs & Free Trade Agreements: Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP - India opted out over China surge & ratchet clauses), IPEF, CPTPP, India-EFTA TEPA, India-UAE CEPA

Economy.topic: National Income Accounting: GDP, GVA, Factor Cost vs Market Price
Economy.keywords: Real vs Nominal GDP, GVA at basic prices, PPP comparisons, Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF)

sub_items.text: GDP Calculation: Expenditure Method ($C + I + G + (X - M)$) vs Income Method vs Output/Production Method (GVA); Real GDP (constant prices base 2011-12, adjusted for inflation) vs Nominal GDP (current prices)
GDP Deflator: $Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) 	imes 100$; comprehensive measure of economy-wide inflation covering all domestic goods and services
Factor Cost vs Market Price: $GVA_{MP} = GVA_{FC} + 	ext{Net Product Taxes (Taxes - Subsidies)}$; GDP is now officially reported as GDP at Market Prices

Gross National Product (GNP): $GNP = GDP + 	ext{Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)}$; Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost is the true measure of National Income ($NNP = GNP - 	ext{Depreciation}$)
Potential GDP & Output Gap: Output Gap = Actual GDP minus Potential GDP; positive gap fuels demand-pull inflation, negative gap signals idle capacity
Gini Coefficient & Lorenz Curve: Graphical representation of wealth/income distribution; 0 = perfect equality, 1 = absolute inequality

Economy.keywords: NPCI products (UPI, AePS, RuPay), Central Bank Digital Currency (Digital Rupee), Account Aggregator

sub_items.text: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e₹): Sovereign legal tender issued by RBI on distributed ledger; Wholesale (e₹-W for interbank G-Sec settlement) vs Retail (e₹-R for public consumer payments); Non-interest bearing direct central bank liability

Unified Payments Interface (UPI): Developed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India - non-profit under Sec 8 Companies Act set up by RBI & IBA); IMPS-based immediate round-the-clock settlement
Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC): Non-profit initiative by DPIIT to unbundle e-commerce, open protocols for discoverability and transactions without platform lock-in
Account Aggregator (AA) Ecosystem: RBI-regulated Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFC-AA) facilitating consent-based financial data sharing without storing data
Financial Action Task Force (FATF): Global money laundering and terror financing watchdog; Grey list (increased monitoring) vs Black list (high risk jurisdictions); Mutual Evaluation of India (2024)
P2P Lending & Neo-banks: RBI guidelines on NBFC-P2P; digital-only banking platforms operating via partner scheduled commercial banks

Economy.keywords: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), Tendulkar & Rangarajan committees, HDI indicators

sub_items.text: Poverty Estimation Committees: Lakdawala (1993 - calorie basket 2400 rural / 2100 urban) $\rightarrow$ Tendulkar (2009 - mixed reference period, consumption basket including health & education, ₹27/day rural ₹33/day urban) $\rightarrow$ Rangarajan (2014 - ₹32 rural / ₹47 urban)

Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI): NITI Aayog National MPI based on Alkire-Foster methodology; 3 dimensions (Health, Education, Standard of Living) and 12 indicators (added Maternal Health & Bank Accounts to Oxford model)
Human Development Index (HDI - UNDP): 3 dimensions: Long and healthy life (Life expectancy at birth), Knowledge (Mean & Expected years of schooling), Decent standard of living (GNI per capita PPP$)
Inequality Adjusted HDI (IHDI), Gender Development Index (GDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII)
Social Protection Schemes: PM-KISAN (direct income support ₹6,000/yr), PM-AWAS Yojana, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (₹5 lakh secondary/tertiary health cover), Jal Jeevan Mission
Labour Force Metrics: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS - MoSPI); Usual Status (ps+ss) vs Current Weekly Status (CWS); Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR)

Environment.topic: Protected Areas: National Parks, Tiger Reserves, Biosphere Reserves
Environment.keywords: Nilgiri Biosphere, Agasthyamalai, Project Tiger, NTCA, Wildlife Corridors, Core vs Buffer zones

sub_items.text: National Parks vs Wildlife Sanctuaries vs Biosphere Reserves: NP (highest protection, NO human grazing or private rights allowed, created under WPA 1972) vs WLS (certain grazing and traditional rights permitted by Chief Wildlife Warden) vs BR (MAB UNESCO zonation: Core, Buffer, Transition)

Tiger Reserves in India: Declared under Wildlife Protection Act (Amendment 2006) on NTCA recommendation; Core/Critical Tiger Habitat (under WPA) vs Buffer area; Inviolable core free of human settlements
Project Tiger & Project Elephant Merger: Overseen by Project Tiger and Elephant Division under MoEFCC; Elephant corridors and MIKE (Monitoring of Illegal Killing of Elephants) sites

Biosphere Reserves in UNESCO MAB Network: 12 out of 18 Indian Biosphere Reserves in World Network (Nilgiri first 2000, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Nokrek, Pachmarhi, Similipal, Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Great Nicobar, Agasthyamala, Khangchendzonga, Panna)
Community Reserves & Conservation Reserves: Introduced in WPA 2002 amendment; Conservation Reserves on govt land adjacent to NPs; Community Reserves on private/community land with community consent
Sacred Groves & Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs): ESZs notified around National Parks under Environment Protection Act 1986 (10 km shock absorber radius default)

Environment.keywords: Critically Endangered species in India (Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Hangul), Prosopis juliflora, Water hyacinth

sub_items.text: IUCN Red List Categories: Extinct (EX), Critically Endangered (CR - 90% decline in 10 yrs or <250 mature individuals), Endangered (EN), Vulnerable (VU), Near Threatened (NT), Least Concern (LC)

Critically Endangered Species of India: Great Indian Bustard (GIB - collision with power lines, Project GIB), Bengal Florican, Gharial (Chambal river), Hangul (Kashmir Stag - Dachigam NP), Pygmy Hog (Manas NP)
Invasive Alien Species: Lantana camara, Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), Prosopis juliflora, Parthenium hysterophorus, African Apple Snail, Senna spectabilis

Keystone Species vs Flagship Species vs Umbrella Species: Keystone (disproportionate impact on ecosystem structure e.g. Fig trees, sea otters, top predators) vs Flagship (charismatic symbol for conservation e.g. Tiger, Panda) vs Indicator (sensitive to environmental change e.g. Lichens for SO2)

Biodiversity Hotspots: Defined by Norman Myers (must contain $\ge$ 1,500 endemic vascular plants and lost $\ge$ 70% primary vegetation); 4 in India: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar)
Ex-situ vs In-situ Conservation: In-situ (National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Sacred Groves) vs Ex-situ (Botanical Gardens, Zoological Parks, Seed Banks, Cryopreservation, Gene Banks)

Environment.topic: International Environmental Treaties: UNFCCC, CBD, CITES, CMS
Environment.keywords: Paris Agreement (NDCs), Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (30x30 target), COP summits

sub_items.text: UNFCCC & Paris Agreement: Goal to limit warming well below 2°C, pursue 1.5°C; Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs); India's 5 Panchamrit targets (500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, 50% energy from renewables, reduce 1 bn tonne carbon emissions, reduce emissions intensity by 45%, Net Zero by 2070)

Carbon Markets under Paris Agreement: Article 6.2 (bilateral ITMOs - Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes) vs Article 6.4 (centralized multilateral carbon crediting mechanism replacing CDM)

Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD): 3 objectives (conservation, sustainable use, fair & equitable benefit sharing); Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (Living Modified Organisms - LMOs) & Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS); Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (30x30 target by 2030)

CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species): Appendix I (threatened with extinction, commercial trade banned), Appendix II (trade strictly regulated), Appendix III (species listed at request of a party)
Convention on Migratory Species (CMS / Bonn Convention): Protects terrestrial, aquatic and avian migratory species across range states; Central Asian Flyway (CAF) National Action Plan

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (1971): Conservation and wise use; Montreux Record (register of wetland sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change - Keoladeo & Loktak in India; Chilika was removed)

Environment.keywords: Wild Life Protection Amendment Act 2022 (4 schedules), EPA 1986, Forest Rights Act 2006, CAMPA

sub_items.text: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 & Amendment 2022: Rationalized schedules from 6 to 4 (Schedule I: highest protection animals, Schedule II: lesser protection, Schedule III: protected plants, Schedule IV: CITES specimens); empowered Central Govt to regulate invasive alien species; CITES Management & Scientific Authorities

Environment (Protection) Act 1986: Umbrella legislation enacted under Article 253 post-Bhopal gas leak; empowers Central Govt to set standards, close polluting units, create authorities (e.g. Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee - GEAC, Coastal Zone Management Authority - CZMA)

Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023: Narrowed scope to recorded government forests; exempted border areas (within 100 km of international borders) for national security projects; renaming to Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam

Biological Diversity Act 2002 & Amendment 2023: 3-tier structure: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA - Chennai), State Biodiversity Boards (SBB), Biodiversity Management Committees (BMC) at panchayat level; Peoples Biodiversity Register (PBR); AYUSH exemptions

Forest Rights Act 2006 (FRA): Recognizes individual forest rights (IFR) up to 4 hectares and community forest rights (CFR) of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFD - 75 years / 3 generations residence); Gram Sabha is the final authority to initiate verification

National Green Tribunal (NGT Act 2010): Established under Art 21 right to healthy environment; specializes in environmental disputes; bound by principles of Natural Justice, NOT Civil Procedure Code (CPC); 6-month disposal mandate

Environment.topic: Pollution, Waste Management Rules & Air Quality Monitoring
Environment.keywords: Plastic Waste Management Rules (EPR), E-waste rules, PM2.5/PM10, Bio-medical waste categories, Fly ash rules

sub_items.text: Air Quality Metrics: National Air Quality Index (AQI - 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb); National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS - 12 pollutants: 8 AQI + Benzene, Benzo(a)pyrene, Arsenic, Nickel); Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) in NCR
Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP): Stage I (Poor 201-300), Stage II (Very Poor 301-400), Stage III (Severe 401-450), Stage IV (Severe+ >450); BS-VI vehicular emission norms (low sulfur 10 ppm)

Plastic Waste Management Rules (Amendment 2022): Ban on identified single-use plastics (SUPs) with low utility and high littering potential (<120 microns); Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mandatory targets and trading certificates
Solid Waste Management Rules 2016: Segregation at source into bio-degradable, dry, and domestic hazardous waste; Bio-mining and bioremediation of legacy dumpsites
E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022: Covers 106 electrical and electronic equipment categories; solar PV modules included; EPR framework with digital exchange credits
Biomedical Waste & Hazardous Waste Rules: Color-coded bin segregation (Yellow: anatomical/soiled, Red: contaminated recyclable plastics, White: sharps, Blue: glassware/metallic implants)

Environment.topic: Ecosystem Concepts, Food Webs & Ecological Succession
Environment.keywords: Inverted biomass pyramid in aquatic ecosystems, Bioaccumulation vs Biomagnification, Primary vs Secondary succession

sub_items.text: Ecosystem Trophic Levels: Autotrophs (producers) $\rightarrow$ Herbivores (primary consumers) $\rightarrow$ Carnivores $\rightarrow$ Apex predators; Lindeman's 10% Law of energy transfer (90% lost as metabolic heat at each trophic step)

Ecological Pyramids: Pyramid of Energy is ALWAYS upright; Pyramid of Biomass is upright in terrestrial ecosystems, but INVERTED in aquatic ecosystems (phytoplankton turn over rapidly); Pyramid of Numbers can be inverted (single tree supporting many birds/parasites)

Bioaccumulation vs Biomagnification: Bioaccumulation (increase in contaminant concentration in an organism over its lifetime from food/water) vs Biomagnification (progressive increase in concentration across trophic levels e.g. DDT, Methylmercury in Minamata disease)

Ecological Succession: Primary succession (starts on bare rock/lava with pioneer species like lichens/mosses) vs Secondary succession (starts where soil already exists post-fire/flood, faster); Seral stages $\rightarrow$ Climax community

Ecotone & Edge Effect: Zone of junction/transition between two ecosystems (e.g. mangrove, marshland, forest edge); Edge species show higher population density and species richness than either adjoining community

Ecosystem Services (Millennium Ecosystem Assessment): Provisioning (food, freshwater, timber), Regulating (climate regulation, flood control, carbon sequestration), Supporting (nutrient cycling, soil formation, primary production), Cultural (recreation, ecotourism)

Environment.topic: Wetlands Conservation & Ramsar Sites in India
Environment.keywords: Montreux Record (Keoladeo, Loktak), Peatlands, Mangrove ecosystems (Sundarbans, Bhitarkanika), Blue Flag beaches

sub_items.text: Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017: State Wetland Authorities; Prohibits reclamation, new industries, solid waste dumping, untreated effluent discharge; excludes river channels, paddy fields, coastal aquaculture ponds

Ramsar Sites in India: 85+ designated wetlands (Tamil Nadu has highest number, followed by UP); Largest Ramsar site: Sundarbans; Smallest: Renuka Wetland (Himachal Pradesh); First designated: Chilika Lake & Keoladeo National Park (1981)
Montreux Record Sites: Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur - famous for Phumdis and endangered Sangai deer); Chilika Lake was removed after successful restoration

Mangrove Ecosystems & MISHTI Scheme: Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes; halophytic plants with pneumatophores (breathing roots), stilt roots, vivipary germination; Sundarbans, Bhitarkanika (Odisha), Pichavaram (TN)
Amrit Dharohar Scheme: Launched for conservation of existing Ramsar sites to promote eco-tourism, carbon sink enhancement and local livelihood generation

Coral Reefs of India: Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep (atolls), Malvan (Maharashtra); Coral bleaching caused by thermal stress (loss of symbiotic zooxanthellae algae)

Environment.topic: Climate Change Mechanisms, Carbon Markets & Geo-engineering
Environment.keywords: Carbon credits, Article 6 of Paris Agreement, Ocean fertilization, Stratospheric aerosol injection, Ocean acidification

sub_items.text: Greenhouse Effect & Global Warming Potential (GWP): Carbon dioxide (CO2, baseline 1, long atmospheric lifetime), Methane (CH4, GWP ~28-36 over 100 yrs, short-lived), Nitrous oxide (N2O, GWP ~273), Fluorinated gases (HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3 with high GWP up to 24,000)
Kigali Amendment to Montreal Protocol: Phasedown of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs - greenhouse gases replacing ozone-depleting CFCs/HCFCs); legally binding targets
Carbon Capture, Utilisation & Storage (CCUS): Point-source capture from thermal plants $\rightarrow$ geological sequestration in saline aquifers or depleted oil fields; Direct Air Capture (DAC)

Carbon Credits & Offsets: 1 carbon credit = 1 metric ton of CO2 equivalent reduced/sequestered; Compliance carbon market vs Voluntary carbon market (VCM); Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 enabling Indian Carbon Market (ICM)

Geo-engineering Techniques: Solar Radiation Management (SRM - stratospheric aerosol injection, marine cloud brightening, space reflectors) vs Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR - ocean iron fertilization, enhanced weathering, biochar, afforestation)

Ocean Acidification: Uptake of anthropogenic CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering seawater pH and carbonate ion saturation ($CO_3^{2-}$), dissolving calcium carbonate shells of calcifying marine organisms

Environment.topic: Sustainable Agriculture: SRI, Natural Farming & Biochar
Environment.keywords: System of Rice Intensification (SRI methane reduction), Zero Budget Natural Farming (Jeevamrutha), Biochar in soil

sub_items.text: System of Rice Intensification (SRI): Less water (alternate wetting and drying), wider spacing, single young seedling per hill, mechanical weeding; Reduces water use by 30-50% and methane emissions by up to 40%

Natural Farming (Bhartiya Prakritik Krishi Paddhati / ZBNF): Subhash Palekar model; 4 pillars: Bijamrit (seed treatment with cow dung/urine), Jiwamrit (fermented soil inoculant), Mulching (straw/crop residue), Waaphasa (soil aeration / moisture condition)
Biochar & Soil Carbon Sequestration: Pyrolysis of agricultural biomass into recalcitrant carbon; improves cation exchange capacity (CEC), water retention, locks carbon for centuries
Zero Tillage Agriculture: Sowing directly into crop residues without plowing (Happy Seeder / Super Seeder); conserves soil moisture, prevents stubble burning, reduces diesel costs
Agroforestry & Permaculture: Integration of trees with agricultural crops and livestock; National Agroforestry Policy 2014; Nitrogen-fixing legumes and shelterbelts
Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) vs Puddled Transplantation: Pre-germinated seeds drilled directly into field; saves nursery labor and groundwater puddling

Environment.topic: Biogeochemical Cycles: Carbon, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Sulphur
Environment.keywords: Gaseous vs Sedimentary cycles, Nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium, Azotobacter), Phosphorus cycle weathering

sub_items.text: Carbon Cycle: Fast biological carbon cycle (photosynthesis and respiration) vs Slow geological carbon cycle (weathering of rocks, sedimentation, fossil fuel formation, subduction volcanism); Oceanic carbon pump (solubility pump & biological pump)

Nitrogen Cycle & Nitrogen Fixation: Biological Nitrogen Fixation (Rhizobium in legumes, Azotobacter free-living aerobic, Clostridium anaerobic, Anabaena cyanobacteria) converts $N_2$ to $NH_3$; Nitrification ($NH_4^+ \rightarrow NO_2^-$ via Nitrosomonas, $NO_2^- \rightarrow NO_3^-$ via Nitrobacter); Denitrification ($NO_3^- \rightarrow N_2$ via Pseudomonas); Eutrophication from agricultural runoff

Phosphorus Cycle: Sedimentary cycle (NO significant atmospheric gas phase); reservoir in phosphate rocks and ocean sediments; weathering releases orthophosphate; limiting nutrient in freshwater bodies

Sulphur Cycle: Combined sedimentary and gaseous cycle; entered into atmosphere via volcanic emissions, biological dimethyl sulfide (DMS) from marine algae, and fossil fuel burning ($SO_2$); causes acid rain ($H_2SO_4$)
Water Cycle & Residence Times: Atmospheric water vapor, oceanic reservoir (97.2%), glaciers/ice caps (2.1%), groundwater (0.65%); Evapotranspiration and precipitation balances

Acid Rain Chemistry: Formed by atmospheric reaction of sulfur dioxide ($SO_2$) and nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$) with water vapor forming sulfuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) and nitric acid ($HNO_3$); pH < 5.6; causes stone leprosy on monuments (marble $CaCO_3$ converts to gypsum $CaSO_4$)

Geography.topic: Indian Drainage System: Himalayan vs Peninsular River Networks
Geography.keywords: Indus tributaries (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Ganga & Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery left/right banks

sub_items.text: Himalayan vs Peninsular River Systems: Antecedent & dendritic drainage vs Superimposed & trellis drainage; Perennial snow-fed vs Monsoonal rain-fed; Youthful gorges & meanders vs Mature graded valleys

Indus River Network: Source at Bokhar Chu glacier near Lake Manasarovar; Left-bank tributaries: Zaskar, Suru, Jhelum (originates Verinag, flows through Wular Lake), Chenab (Chandra + Bhaga at Tandi, largest tributary), Ravi (Rohtang Pass), Beas (Beas Kund, entirely within India), Sutlej (Rakas Lake); Right-bank: Shyok, Gilgit, Hunza, Kabul; Indus Waters Treaty 1960 (India has exclusive rights over Eastern rivers: Ravi, Beas, Sutlej; Pakistan over Western rivers: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab with specified Indian run-of-the-river rights)

Ganga River Network: Origin as Bhagirathi at Gaumukh (Gangotri glacier); Confluences (Panch Prayag): Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), Nandaprayag (Alaknanda + Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Alaknanda + Pindar), Rudraprayag (Alaknanda + Mandakini), Devprayag (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi = Ganga); Left-bank: Ramganga, Gomti (originates in plain Gomat Taal), Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi (Saptakoshi), Mahananda; Right-bank: Yamuna (originates Yamunotri, joined by Chambal, Sind, Betwa, Ken), Son (originates Amarkantak plateau), Punpun, Damodar

Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo): Origin at Chemayungdung glacier near Manasarovar; enters India via Great Bend (Namcha Barwa gorge) as Siang/Dihang; joined by Dibang and Lohit near Sadiya; Left-bank: Dhansiri, Burhi Dihing; Right-bank: Subansiri, Kameng, Manas, Sankosh, Teesta; Majuli river island; enters Bangladesh as Jamuna $\rightarrow$ joins Padma $\rightarrow$ joins Meghna into Bay of Bengal

Peninsular East-Flowing Rivers: Mahanadi (Sihawa hills in Chhattisgarh, Hirakud dam), Godavari (Dakshin Ganga, originates Trimbakeshwar in Western Ghats, tributaries: Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga $\rightarrow$ Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari, Manjra right-bank), Krishna (originates Mahabaleshwar, tributaries: Tungabhadra, Bhima, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Musi), Cauvery (originates Brahmagiri hills in Kodagu, tributaries: Harangi, Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathi left-bank; Lakshmantirtha, Kabini, Bhavani, Noyyal, Amaravati right-bank; Shivanasamudra falls)

Peninsular West-Flowing Rivers: Narmada (originates Amarkantak plateau, flows through rift valley between Vindhyas and Satpuras, Dhuandhar falls in marble rocks, Sardar Sarovar dam, forms estuary), Tapti (originates Multai in Betul district, flows between Satpura and Ajanta ranges), Sabarmati, Mahi (crosses Tropic of Cancer twice), Luni (inland drainage ending in Rann of Kutch), Periyar & Bharathapuzha (Kerala), Mandovi & Zuari (Goa)

Geography.topic: Climatology: Indian Monsoon Dynamics, Jet Streams & ENSO
Geography.core_sources: NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography
Geography.keywords: ITCZ movement, Somali Jet, Tibetan heating, El Niño/La Niña, Indian Ocean Dipole (Positive/Negative IOD)

sub_items.text: Mechanism of Indian Monsoon: Thermal contrast between Indian subcontinent and Indian Ocean; Shift of Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) northwards to Tibetan Plateau in summer (Monsoon Trough); Heating of Tibetan Plateau creating high-level anticyclone and Tropical Easterly Jet (TEJ) over peninsular India; Somali Low-Level Jet (Findlater Jet)

Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream (SWJS): Bifurcated by Tibetan Plateau in winter (southern branch over northern India brings Western Disturbances from Mediterranean causing winter rain to wheat crops); withdrawal of southern branch triggers summer monsoon onset over Kerala

El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO): Walker Circulation in tropical Pacific; El Niño (warm phase: warming of eastern Pacific, weakening of Walker cell, atmospheric pressure rises over Darwin, historically correlates with weak/deficient Indian monsoon) vs La Niña (cold phase: strong trade winds, warm pool pushed to western Pacific, favorable for Indian monsoon); Southern Oscillation Index (SOI = Tahiti pressure minus Darwin pressure; negative SOI = El Niño)

Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD): Sea surface temperature anomaly between western equatorial Indian Ocean and eastern Indian Ocean (near Indonesia); Positive IOD (warmer western Indian Ocean $\rightarrow$ enhances Indian monsoon and offsets El Niño negative effect); Negative IOD (colder western Indian Ocean $\rightarrow$ depresses Indian monsoon)

Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO): Intra-seasonal eastward propagating wave of cloudiness and rainfall along equator (30-60 day cycle); enhances monsoon precipitation when active phase sits over Indian Ocean

Retreating Monsoon & North-East Monsoon: Withdrawal starts from north-west India in September; October Heat caused by high temperature and high humidity; North-East Monsoon (Oct-Dec) picks moisture over Bay of Bengal and causes heavy rainfall in coastal Tamil Nadu and Coromandel Coast

Geography.topic: World Geography: Strategic Chokepoints, Seas & Conflict Borders
Geography.keywords: Mediterranean Sea bordering nations, Black Sea, Red Sea (Bab-el-Mandeb), Strait of Hormuz, Strait of Malacca, Sahel region

sub_items.text: Maritime Chokepoints & Strategic Straits: Strait of Malacca (between Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, connects Indian Ocean to South China Sea), Strait of Hormuz (between Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, critical oil transit), Bab-el-Mandeb (between Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, gate to Suez Canal), Bosphorus & Dardanelles (Turkish straits connecting Black Sea to Mediterranean), Suez Canal, Panama Canal, Sunda and Lombok Straits

Seas & Bordering Nations: Black Sea (Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey, Ukraine - mnemonic: BGR RTU), Caspian Sea (Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia, Turkmenistan - mnemonic: TARIK), Red Sea (Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti - mnemonic: DESSEY), Mediterranean Sea, Baltic Sea, Persian Gulf

Active Geopolitical Conflict Geographies: West Asia (Gaza Strip, West Bank, Golan Heights, Sinai Peninsula, Negev desert, Litani river in Lebanon); Horn of Africa & Sahel region (Sudan, South Sudan, Chad, Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso); South China Sea (Nine-Dash Line, Spratly Islands, Paracel Islands, Scarborough Shoal)

Landlocked Countries & Transit Corridors: Central Asian Republics (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan double-landlocked, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan); International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC - Mumbai to St. Petersburg via Bandar Abbas & Chabahar); India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)

Strategic Islands & Territories: Diego Garcia (Chagos Archipelago), Socotra (Yemen), Reunion Island (France), Cocos (Keeling) Islands (Australia), Kuril Islands (Russia-Japan dispute), Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands (Japan-China dispute)
Boundary Lines: Radcliffe Line (India-Pakistan), McMahon Line (India-China Arunachal sector), Durand Line (Pakistan-Afghanistan), Line of Actual Control (LAC) vs Line of Control (LoC)

Geography.keywords: Zoji La, Nathu La, Shipki La, Lipulekh, Western Ghats vs Eastern Ghats gaps (Palghat, Thalghat, Bhorghat)

sub_items.text: Geological Divisions of India: The Peninsular Block (ancient stable crystalline shield since Archean times), The Himalayas and other Peninsular Mountains (young fold mountains of Tertiary origin), Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain (aggradational depositional basin)

Himalayan Longitudinal Zones: Trans-Himalayas (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar ranges; K2 Godwin-Austen, Siachen glacier) $\rightarrow$ Greater Himalayas / Himadri (average elevation 6,000 m; Everest, Kanchenjunga, Nanda Devi; crystalline core) $\rightarrow$ Lesser Himalayas / Himachal (Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Nag Tibba, Mahabharat ranges; hill stations) $\rightarrow$ Shiwaliks (outermost foothills; Duns like Dehradun and Duars)

Peninsular Plateaus & Hills: Aravalli Range (relict ancient fold mountain, highest peak Guru Shikhar on Mount Abu), Vindhyan Range, Satpura Range (horst mountain: Dhupgarh peak, flanked by Narmada and Tapti), Western Ghats (Sahyadri, continuous escarpment; passes: Thalghat, Bhorghat, Palghat gap between Nilgiris and Annamalai; Anamudi highest peak in South India in Anaimalai hills), Eastern Ghats (discontinuous, eroded by rivers; Jindhagada/Arma Konda peak; Nilgiri Hills where Western and Eastern Ghats meet, Doddabetta peak)

Northern Plains Morphological Zones: Bhabar (narrow 8-10 km pebble belt along Shiwalik foothills where streams disappear underground) $\rightarrow$ Terai (marshy, damp, heavily forested tract where streams re-emerge) $\rightarrow$ Bhangar (older alluvial terrace above flood plains, contains calcareous kankar deposits) $\rightarrow$ Khadar (newer flood plain alluvium, fertile, enriched annually)

Strategic Mountain Passes: Zoji La (Srinagar to Leh), Banihal Pass (Jawaharlal Tunnel, Jammu to Srinagar), Khardung La (Leh to Nubra valley), Rohtang & Atal Tunnel (Kullu to Lahaul-Spiti), Bara Lacha La (Himachal to Ladakh), Shipki La (Sutlej enters India, Himachal to Tibet), Mana & Niti Passes (Uttarakhand to Tibet), Nathu La & Jelep La (Sikkim to Tibet), Bomdi La (Arunachal Pradesh)

Coastal Plains & Islands: Western Coastal Plains (narrow, submerged coast, lagoons/kayals in Malabar, natural ports) vs Eastern Coastal Plains (emergent coast, broad deltas, shallow water); Andaman and Nicobar Islands (volcanic/tectonic continuation of Arakan Yoma; Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman and Nicobar; Duncan Passage separates South and Little Andaman; Barren Island only active volcano; Indira Point southernmost tip); Lakshadweep Islands (coral atolls; Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from main Lakshadweep; Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from Maldives)

Geography.keywords: Black cotton soil (regur, moisture retention), Laterite soil (leached, acidic), Major crops (Rice, Wheat, Cotton, Tea, Coffee climatic criteria)

sub_items.text: Major Soil Types of India (ICAR Classification): Alluvial Soils (largest group ~40%, rich in potash, deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus, divided into Khadar and Bhangar), Black Soils / Regur (formed by weathering of Deccan basalt lava, rich in clay, iron, lime, self-ploughing property with deep cracks in dry season, ideal for cotton), Red and Yellow Soils (derived from crystalline Archean rocks, rich in iron peroxide giving red color, deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, humus), Laterite Soils (formed under high temperature and heavy leaching rainfall, rich in bauxite and iron oxide, acidic, cashew nuts and tapioca), Arid / Desert Soils (sandy, saline, low moisture and humus, kankar layer), Saline Soils / Usara (contain high sodium, magnesium, potassium due to poor drainage and canal over-irrigation)

Cropping Seasons of India: Kharif (monsoon crops, sown June-July, harvested Sept-Oct: rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soybean), Rabi (winter crops, sown Oct-Dec, harvested April-June: wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas), Zaid (short summer season March-June: watermelon, cucumber, fodder crops)

Major Crops Distribution: Rice (staple, high rainfall >100 cm, WB, UP, Punjab leading; SRI method), Wheat (cool growing season, 50-75 cm rain, UP, Punjab, MP, Haryana), Millets / Nutri-Cereals (coarse grains, drought-resistant, Jowar in Maharashtra, Bajra in Rajasthan, Ragi in Karnataka; International Year of Millets 2023), Cotton (black soil, 210 frost-free days, Gujarat, Maharashtra), Sugarcane (tropical and subtropical, high water, UP, Maharashtra), Tea (acidic soil, hill slopes, Assam, Darjeeling, Nilgiris), Coffee (Arabica and Robusta, shade trees, Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala, TN)

Irrigation Systems in India: Wells and Tubewells (largest source ~62% of irrigated area, leading to groundwater depletion), Canals (second largest ~26%, dominant in Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan), Tanks (traditional in Peninsular hard rock terrain, TN, Andhra Pradesh); Micro-irrigation (Drip and Sprinkler under PMKSY - Per Drop More Crop)

Soil Degradation & Conservation: Soil erosion (sheet erosion by runoff water, rill erosion, gully erosion in Chambal ravines), Salinization and waterlogging in canal-irrigated green revolution belts; Conservation methods: Contour plowing, terracing, strip cropping, shelterbelts, mulching, check dams
Agro-Climatic Zones: Planning Commission delineated 15 agro-climatic zones based on topography, rainfall, temperature, cropping systems and water resources

Geography.keywords: Gondwana Coal basins (Damodar, Mahanadi), Iron ore belts (Bailadila, Kudremukh), Bauxite, Lithium deposits (J&K)

sub_items.text: Mineral Belts of India: North-Eastern Peninsular Belt (richest mineral belt, Chotanagpur plateau, covers Jharkhand, Odisha, WB; iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite, mica), Central Belt (Chhattisgarh, MP, Andhra, Maharashtra; bauxite, iron ore, limestone), Southern Belt (Karnataka, TN; iron ore, bauxite, lignite coal), North-Western Belt (Rajasthan, Gujarat; non-ferrous minerals, copper, zinc, petroleum, marble), South-Western Belt (Goa, south Karnataka; iron ore)

Iron Ore Distribution: Haematite (high grade ~60-70% Fe, Odisha: Mayurbhanj, Kendujhar; Jharkhand: Singhbhum; Chhattisgarh: Bailadila) vs Magnetite (black ore with magnetic properties ~70% Fe, Karnataka: Kudremukh, Bellary; Andhra Pradesh)

Coal Reserves & Types: Anthracite (highest carbon >80%, Jammu & Kashmir small reserves), Bituminous (dominant in India ~70-80% carbon, Gondwana coalfields ~250 million years old in Damodar, Mahanadi, Godavari valleys: Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro), Lignite (brown coal, Neyveli in Tamil Nadu), Peat (initial stage of coalification); Tertiary coal in North-East (Assam, Meghalaya, high sulfur content); Coal Gasification & Coal Bed Methane (CBM)

Petroleum & Natural Gas Basins: Category I Producing Basins: Mumbai Offshore (Bombay High), Cambay Basin (Ankleshwar), Assam Shelf (Digboi oldest oil field, Naharkatiya), Krishna-Godavari (KG-D6 offshore basin, Ravva), Barmer Basin (Rajasthan - Mangala, Bhagyam); Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR - Visakhapatnam, Mangalore, Padur, Chandikhol managed by ISPRL)

Critical Minerals & Non-Ferrous Metals: Critical Minerals Strategy (30 identified minerals including Lithium in Reasi J&K and Katghora Chhattisgarh, Cobalt, Nickel, Rare Earth Elements - REEs); Bauxite (Odisha largest producer: Panchpatmali), Copper (Khetri in Rajasthan, Malanjkhand in MP), Lead & Zinc (Zawar mines in Udaipur Rajasthan)

Industrial Regions of India: Mumbai-Pune Industrial Region, Hugli Industrial Region, Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu Region, Gujarat Industrial Region, Chotanagpur Industrial Region, Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut Region, Visakhapatnam-Guntur Region, Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram Region

Geography.topic: Oceanography: Ocean Currents, Tides & Coral Reefs
Geography.keywords: Warm vs Cold ocean currents (Kuroshio/Oyashio, Gulf Stream, Humboldt), Upwelling zones, Coral bleaching triggers

sub_items.text: Ocean Bottom Relief: Continental Shelf (shallow gentle slope 1-2°, richest fishing grounds like Grand Banks and Dogger Bank, offshore petroleum like Bombay High) $\rightarrow$ Continental Slope (steep gradient, submarine canyons) $\rightarrow$ Continental Rise $\rightarrow$ Abyssal Plain (deep ocean floor 3,000-6,000 m, polymetallic nodules) $\rightarrow$ Oceanic Deeps / Trenches (deepest Mariana Trench / Challenger Deep in Pacific, Sunda/Java trench in Indian Ocean; associated with subduction zones)

Ocean Temperature & Salinity Distribution: Thermocline (steep vertical temperature drop layer); Average ocean salinity 35 ppt (parts per thousand); Highest salinity in landlocked seas with high evaporation (Red Sea 41 ppt, Dead Sea 238 ppt, Lake Van 330 ppt); Isohalines and Halocline

Ocean Currents of the World: Atlantic Ocean Currents: Warm: Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Brazil Current; Cold: Labrador Current, Canary Current, Benguela Current, Falkland Current (meeting of Gulf Stream and Labrador forms dense fog and rich fishing near Newfoundland); Pacific Ocean Currents: Warm: Kuroshio Current; Cold: Oyashio/Kamchatka Current, California Current, Peru/Humboldt Current (upwelling zone supporting anchovy fishery); Indian Ocean Currents: Monsoonal reversal of currents (Southwest monsoon drift eastward in summer, Northeast monsoon drift westward in winter); Agulhas Current (warm), West Australian Current (cold)

Tides Mechanism & Types: Gravitational pull of Moon and Sun; Spring Tides (Sun, Moon and Earth in a straight line - Syzygy: Conjunction at New Moon or Opposition at Full Moon; highest tidal range) vs Neap Tides (Sun and Moon at right angles - Quadrature; lowest tidal range); Semi-diurnal tides (two high and two low tides daily) vs Diurnal tides; Tidal bore (Hooghly river)

Coral Reef Formations & Bleaching: Fringing Reefs (attached to coast), Barrier Reefs (separated by wide lagoon like Great Barrier Reef), Atolls (circular/horseshoe reef surrounding central lagoon like Lakshadweep); Coral polyps live in mutualistic symbiosis with photosynthetic Zooxanthellae algae; Bleaching triggered by rise in sea surface temperature (SST >1°C above summer maximum), ocean acidification, UV radiation

Marine Resources & Law of the Sea (UNCLOS): Internal Waters $\rightarrow$ Territorial Sea (up to 12 nautical miles, full sovereignty, innocent passage permitted) $\rightarrow$ Contiguous Zone (12-24 NM, customs, fiscal, immigration enforcement) $\rightarrow$ Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ up to 200 NM, sovereign rights for exploring and exploiting living/non-living natural resources) $\rightarrow$ High Seas (international waters, common heritage of mankind overseen by International Seabed Authority - ISA; India's Deep Ocean Mission and polymetallic nodule exploration in Central Indian Ocean Basin)

Geography.keywords: P-waves vs S-waves shadow zones, Divergent vs Convergent boundaries, Ring of Fire, Karst landforms

sub_items.text: Internal Structure of the Earth: Crust (Continental granitic sial vs Oceanic basaltic sima) $\rightarrow$ Mohorovicic Discontinuity (Moho) $\rightarrow$ Mantle (Asthenosphere plastic upper mantle source of magma) $\rightarrow$ Gutenberg Discontinuity $\rightarrow$ Outer Core (liquid iron-nickel generating geomagnetic geodynamo) $\rightarrow$ Lehmann Discontinuity $\rightarrow$ Inner Core (solid iron-nickel nife)

Continental Drift Theory (Alfred Wegener 1912): Supercontinent Pangaea surrounded by giant ocean Panthalassa; Evidence: Jig-saw fit of South America and Africa, Palaeoclimatic evidence (tillite deposits in Gondwana continents), Fossil distribution (Glossopteris flora, Mesosaurus reptile), Placer deposits of gold in Ghana coast from Brazil

Seafloor Spreading & Paleomagnetism (Harry Hess 1960): Upwelling of magma along Mid-Oceanic Ridges creates new oceanic crust; Magnetic striping and geomagnetic reversals symmetrical across ridge; Oceanic crust is much younger than continental crust (<200 million years)

Plate Tectonics Theory: Lithospheric plates floating on asthenosphere; 7 Major Plates (Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian, Antarctic) and Minor Plates (Nazca, Cocos, Arabian, Philippine, Caribbean, Juan de Fuca); Plate Boundaries: Divergent (constructive: Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East African Rift Valley), Convergent (destructive: Oceanic-Continental forming Andes, Oceanic-Oceanic forming island arcs/trenches like Marianas, Continental-Continental forming Himalayas), Transform (conservative: San Andreas Fault)

Earthquakes & Seismic Waves: Focus / Hypocenter (point of origin inside earth) vs Epicenter (point on surface vertically above focus); Body Waves: P-waves (Primary, compressional/longitudinal, travel through solid, liquid, gas, fastest) vs S-waves (Secondary, shear/transverse, travel through SOLIDS ONLY, cannot pass through liquid outer core, creates wide S-wave shadow zone beyond 105°); Surface Waves (L-waves and Rayleigh waves, slowest, cause maximum surface damage); Measurement: Richter Scale (magnitude/energy released, logarithmic) vs Mercalli Scale (intensity/visible damage, 1-12)

Volcanism & Volcanic Landforms: Intrusive Landforms: Batholiths (large deep granitic plutons), Laccoliths (dome-shaped with pipe feeder), Lopoliths (saucer-shaped), Phacoliths (anticline/syncline crests), Sills (horizontal sheets), Dykes (vertical wall-like intrusions); Extrusive Landforms: Shield Volcanoes (basaltic fluid lava, gentle slope e.g. Hawaiian volcanoes), Composite Volcanoes / Stratovolcanoes (viscous andesitic/felsic lava, pyroclastic explosions e.g. Mt Fuji, Mt Vesuvius), Calderas (collapsed volcanic crater e.g. Krakatoa, Lonar lake is meteor impact), Flood Basalt Provinces (Deccan Traps)

Geography.topic: Major Ports, Inland Waterways & Transport Corridors
Geography.keywords: 12 Major Ports of India, Landlord port model, National Waterway 1 (Ganga), Dedicated Freight Corridors (EDFC/WDFC)

sub_items.text: Major Ports of India: 12 Major Ports under Central Major Port Authorities Act 2021 + 200+ non-major ports under State Maritime Boards; West Coast Ports: Deendayal / Kandla (Gujarat, tidal port, free trade zone), Mumbai Port (natural deep harbour), Jawaharlal Nehru Port / Nhava Sheva (largest container port in India), Mormugao (Goa, iron ore export), New Mangalore (Karnataka, Kudremukh iron ore), Cochin Port (Willingdon Island, natural harbour); East Coast Ports: V.O. Chidambaranar / Tuticorin (TN), Chennai Port (artificial harbour, oldest), Kamarajar / Ennore (first corporatized major port), Visakhapatnam Port (deepest landlocked protected harbour), Paradip (Odisha, mechanized iron ore berth), Syama Prasad Mookerjee / Kolkata-Haldia (riverine port on Hooghly river)

National Waterways (National Waterways Act 2016): 111 declared National Waterways; NW-1: Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system (Prayagraj to Haldia, 1620 km, Jal Marg Vikas Project with multi-modal terminals at Varanasi, Sahibganj, Haldia); NW-2: Brahmaputra river (Dhubri to Sadiya, 891 km); NW-3: West Coast Canal (Kottapuram to Kollam with Udyogmandal and Champakara canals in Kerala, 205 km); NW-4: Krishna-Godavari rivers with Buckingham Canal (Kakinada to Puducherry); NW-5: Brahmani river with Matai and East Coast Canal (Odisha)

Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC): Western DFC (Dadri in UP to JNPT Mumbai, 1506 km, electric traction, double-stack container trains) & Eastern DFC (Ludhiana in Punjab to Dankuni in WB, 1875 km, moves coal, finished steel, foodgrains); Subsumed under PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan

National Highway Development Project & Bharatmala Pariyojana: Golden Quadrilateral (connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, 5846 km); North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) & East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar) intersecting at Jhansi; Bharatmala Pariyojana focuses on economic corridors, border and international connectivity roads, coastal and port connectivity roads, expressways

Railway Corridors & Vande Bharat: High Speed Rail (Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train project using Japanese Shinkansen E5 technology); Semi-high speed Vande Bharat trainsets (indigenously developed at Integral Coach Factory Chennai, distributed traction system, Kavach automatic train protection)

Sagarmala Programme: Port modernization and new port development (Vadhavan port in Maharashtra mega port project), Port connectivity enhancement, Port-linked industrialization, Coastal community development

ScienceTech.topic: Space Technology: ISRO Missions, Orbits & Deep Space Astronomy
ScienceTech.keywords: Gaganyaan, Aditya-L1 (Lagrange Point L1), Chandrayaan, James Webb Telescope, LEO vs GEO vs Sun-synchronous orbit

sub_items.text: Orbits & Trajectories: Low Earth Orbit (LEO, 160-2000 km, earth observation, ISS, Starlink), Geostationary Orbit (GEO, circular, exactly 35,786 km above equator, period 24 hours, stationary over one longitude, communication satellites) vs Geosynchronous Orbit (GSO, inclined), Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO, passes over poles, constant solar illumination angle for optical imaging), Lagrange Points (L1 to L5 gravitational equilibrium points; L1 home to Aditya-L1 and SOHO; L2 home to James Webb Space Telescope)

ISRO Launch Vehicles: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle - 4 stages: solid-liquid-solid-liquid, workhorse), GSLV Mk II (3 stages: solid-liquid-cryogenic), LVM3 / GSLV Mk III (heaviest launch vehicle: two S200 solid strap-ons, L110 core liquid stage, C25 cryogenic upper stage; carried Chandrayaan-2/3, Gaganyaan test flights), SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle - 3 solid stages + Velocity Trimming Module for low-cost on-demand launches)

Lunar & Interplanetary Missions: Chandrayaan-3 (historic soft landing near lunar South Pole; Vikram lander and Pragyan rover; detected sulfur with LIBS; ChaSTE thermal probe measured lunar topsoil temperature gradient; SHAPE payload on propulsion module), Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan), Aditya-L1 (seven payloads: VELC solar corona coronagraph, SUIT UV imaging, ASPEX solar wind analyzer)

Gaganyaan Human Spaceflight Programme: Crew Module and Service Module; HLVM3 launcher; Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS); Vyommitra humanoid robot for uncrewed orbital tests; Pad Abort and In-flight Abort tests (TV-D1)

Satellite Navigation Systems: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation / IRNSS - 7 satellites: 3 in GEO + 4 in GSO; operates in L5 and S bands, expanding to L1 frequency for civil mobile integration; covers India + 1500 km around borders) vs GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU), BeiDou (China); GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation for civil aviation)

Space Sector Reforms & Commercial Space: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre - single-window regulator for private space entities), NewSpace India Limited (NSIL - commercial arm of ISRO), Indian Space Policy 2023 opening end-to-end space activities to non-government entities (Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos 3D-printed engine Agnibaan)

ScienceTech.core_sources: NCERT Class 12 Biotech / Down to Earth
ScienceTech.keywords: CRISPR-Cas9, Germline vs Somatic editing, Three-parent baby (Mitochondrial replacement), mRNA vaccines vs viral vector

sub_items.text: Recombinant DNA Technology: Restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors cutting at palindromic sequences) $\rightarrow$ DNA ligase joins fragments $\rightarrow$ Plasmids / vectors carry gene into host bacterium $\rightarrow$ Expression of recombinant proteins (e.g. human insulin / Humulin)

CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats; derived from bacterial adaptive immune system against bacteriophages; Guide RNA (gRNA) directs Cas9 endonuclease enzyme to target DNA sequence for double-strand break; Non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or Homology-directed repair (HDR); Nobel Prize 2020 (Emmanuelle Charpentier & Jennifer Doudna); Cas12/Cas13 variants for RNA editing; Sickle cell gene therapy (Casgevy)

Somatic Cell vs Germline Gene Editing: Somatic editing (changes in non-reproductive cells, treats individual patient, NOT inherited by offspring) vs Germline editing (changes in sperm, egg, or early embryo, inherited by future generations, severe ethical bans globally)

Genetically Modified (GM) Crops in India: Bt Cotton (ONLY commercially approved GM crop in India, carries Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab endotoxin genes from soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis lethal to bollworms); GM Mustard (Dhara Mustard Hybrid-11 / DMH-11 developed by Delhi University using Barnase-Barstar barnase-barstar system for hybridization, approved by GEAC but facing SC litigation); Bt Brinjal (moratorium since 2010); GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee under MoEFCC is apex regulatory body)

Next-Generation Sequencing & Genome India Project: Sanger sequencing $\rightarrow$ High-throughput NGS; Genome India Project (Department of Biotechnology sequenced 10,000 reference genomes of Indian population to map disease prevalence and genetic diversity); Human Genome Project completed reference

Cloning & Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer (SCNT - Dolly the sheep, transferring adult somatic cell nucleus into enucleated oocyte); Three-Parent Baby / Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy (maternal spindle transfer or pronuclear transfer to replace mutated mitochondrial DNA of mother with healthy donor mitochondria, prevents inherited Leigh syndrome)

ScienceTech.keywords: Superbugs, One Health approach, Zoonoses (Nipah, Bird flu), Tuberculosis BPaLM regimen, Sickle Cell Anaemia Mission

sub_items.text: Infectious Disease Pathogens: Viruses (obligate intracellular parasites, DNA or RNA genome, lack cellular machinery, antibiotics INEFFECTIVE; Influenza, HIV, Hepatitis, Polio, Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, COVID-19, Nipah, Ebola) vs Bacteria (single-cell prokaryotes with cell wall; Tuberculosis, Cholera, Typhoid, Plague, Anthrax, Tetanus) vs Fungi (eukaryotes; Mucormycosis/Black fungus, Candidiasis) vs Protozoa (single-cell eukaryotes; Malaria caused by Plasmodium transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito, Kala-azar / Leishmaniasis transmitted by sandfly, Sleeping sickness transmitted by tsetse fly)

Vaccine Platforms & Technologies: Inactivated / Killed Whole Virus (Covaxin, Polio IPV), Live Attenuated (MMR, BCG, Oral Polio OPV), Subunit / Protein Subunit (Novavax, Corbevax, Hepatitis B), Viral Vector (AstraZeneca/Covishield using chimpanzee adenovirus ChadOx1, Sputnik V), mRNA Vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna - deliver lipid nanoparticles containing mRNA encoding viral spike protein, translated by host ribosomes, degraded rapidly without altering genomic DNA), DNA Vaccines (ZyCoV-D plasmid DNA applied needle-free)

Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR): Superbugs developing resistance to antibiotics, antivirals, antifungals due to overuse in human medicine and livestock growth promoters; Mechanisms: enzymatic destruction (beta-lactamases, NDM-1 enzyme), efflux pumps, altered target receptors; Priority pathogen list (carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae); National Action Plan on AMR (One Health approach); Red Line campaign on antibiotic packaging

Tuberculosis & Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs): Mycobacterium tuberculosis; Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB resistant to first-line Isoniazid and Rifampicin) vs Extensively Drug-Resistant TB (XDR-TB resistant to fluoroquinolones and at least one second-line injectable like Bedaquiline/Delamanid); National Strategic Plan to End TB (TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana ₹500/month nutritional incentive); Kala-azar elimination target; Lymphatic Filariasis (elephantiasis transmitted by Culex mosquito)

Zoonotic Spillover & One Health: Diseases jumping from animal hosts to humans (bats reservoirs for Nipah, Ebola, Coronaviruses; avian flu H5N1; swine flu H1N1); One Health Joint Plan of Action integrating human health, animal health, and environmental ecosystems; National One Health Mission

Diagnostic Technologies: RT-PCR (Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction - gold standard for RNA viruses, amplifies cDNA through thermal cycles using Taq polymerase), Rapid Antigen Test (detects viral surface proteins), ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay detects antibodies or antigens), TrueNat (chip-based point-of-care micro-PCR test for TB)

ScienceTech.topic: Information Technology, AI, Quantum Computing & Semiconductors
ScienceTech.keywords: Quantum Qubits & Superposition, Large Language Models (LLMs), Blockchain ledgers, Semiconductor lithography fabrication

sub_items.text: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning: Narrow AI vs General AI (AGI); Machine Learning paradigms: Supervised Learning (labeled training data, classification/regression), Unsupervised Learning (unlabeled data, clustering, PCA), Reinforcement Learning (reward/penalty optimization); Deep Learning & Neural Networks (multi-layered perceptrons, CNNs for image recognition, RNNs/Transformers with self-attention mechanisms powering Large Language Models - LLMs like Gemini, GPT); Diffusion Models for generative media

AI Governance & Safety: Generative AI issues: Hallucinations, algorithmic bias, copyright infringement, deepfakes; IndiaAI Mission (10,000+ GPU supercomputing capacity, foundational models, AI ethics guidelines); Bletchley Park AI Safety Declaration; European Union AI Act (risk-based tiered classification: unacceptable risk banned, high risk strictly audited)

Quantum Computing & Physics Principles: Classical Bit (0 OR 1) vs Quantum Bit / Qubit (0 AND 1 simultaneously via Superposition); Quantum Entanglement (spooky action at a distance, state of one qubit instantaneously determines state of entangled partner); Quantum Decoherence (susceptibility to environmental thermal noise, requiring near absolute zero dilution refrigerators); Quantum Supremacy / Advantage; National Quantum Mission (NQM India - ₹6,000 crore outlay for developing 50-1000 physical qubits in 8 years, quantum communication, quantum key distribution - QKD, quantum sensors)

Semiconductor Fabrication & Chip Design: Silicon crystal wafers $\rightarrow$ Photolithography (Extreme Ultraviolet - EUV lithography using 13.5 nm wavelength pioneered by ASML) $\rightarrow$ Etching and chemical vapor deposition; Process nodes (3 nm, 2 nm nanosheet GAAFET transistors); India Semiconductor Mission (ISM - $10 billion fiscal incentive scheme subsidizing 50% capital cost for semiconductor fabs, display fabs, ATMP/OSAT assembly and testing plants like Dholera and Sanand)

Data Protection & Digital Governance: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023: Data Principal (individual), Data Fiduciary (entity processing data), Consent Managers, Data Protection Board of India; Cross-border data transfers allowed except to blacklisted countries; Exemptions for state security; Right to correction and erasure; Penalties up to ₹250 crore

Blockchain & Web3: Distributed ledger technology; Cryptographic hashing (SHA-256) and consensus mechanisms: Proof of Work (PoW - compute and energy heavy) vs Proof of Stake (PoS - validators stake tokens); Smart Contracts (self-executing automated agreements on Ethereum); Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs); Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP for privacy verification)

ScienceTech.topic: Clean Energy Technologies: Green Hydrogen, Batteries & Fuel Cells
ScienceTech.keywords: Green vs Grey vs Blue hydrogen, PEM Electrolyzers, Sodium-ion vs Lithium-ion batteries, Solid-state batteries

sub_items.text: Green Hydrogen & Electrolysis: Hydrogen color spectrum: Grey Hydrogen (produced from natural gas via steam methane reforming, emits CO2), Blue Hydrogen (grey hydrogen with Carbon Capture & Storage - CCS), Green Hydrogen (water electrolysis using 100% renewable electricity, ZERO greenhouse gas emissions); Electrolyser technologies: Alkaline Electrolysers (mature, KOH liquid electrolyte), Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM - platinum/iridium catalysts, fast response to fluctuating solar/wind power), Solid Oxide Electrolysers (SOEC - high temperature steam); National Green Hydrogen Mission (target 5 MMT per annum by 2030, SIGHT scheme incentives for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production)

Advanced Battery Chemistries & Energy Storage: Lithium-ion Batteries (dominant for EVs; Cathode chemistries: LFP - Lithium Iron Phosphate safe and cobalt-free, NMC - Nickel Manganese Cobalt higher energy density; Anode: graphite; Liquid organic electrolyte); Next-gen batteries: Solid-State Batteries (solid ceramic/polymer electrolyte, eliminating flammable liquid, higher energy density, faster charging), Sodium-ion Batteries (cheaper, abundant sodium, no lithium/cobalt dependencies), Flow Batteries (vanadium redox for long-duration grid storage); Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage

Solar Photovoltaic & Next-Gen Solar Cells: Silicon PV (Monocrystalline higher efficiency ~22% vs Polycrystalline ~16%); Perovskite Solar Cells (tunable bandgap, low production cost, tandem perovskite-silicon cells exceeding 30% laboratory efficiency); International Solar Alliance (ISA - launched by India and France at COP21 Paris, HQ in Gurugram, One Sun One World One Grid - OSOWOG initiative); PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (rooftop solar for 1 crore households)

Biofuels & National Policy on Biofuels: 1st Generation (1G - food crops: sugarcane juice, molasses, damaged foodgrains, broken rice for ethanol), 2nd Generation (2G - non-food biomass: agricultural residue, rice straw, bagasse; 2G ethanol bio-refinery at Panipat), 3rd Generation (3G - algae and aquatic biomass), 4th Generation (4G - genetically engineered microorganisms for carbon capture); Ethanol Blending Programme (achieved 12% blending, target 20% by 2025-26 / E20); Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT - CBG / Compressed Bio-Gas plants from agricultural residue)
