Nuclear Energy & Three-Stage Programme: Homi Bhabha Three-Stage Plan utilizing vast Thorium reserves: Stage 1: Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs - natural uranium fuel, heavy water moderator/coolant, produces Plutonium-239), Stage 2: Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs - PFBR Kalpakkam 500 MWe, liquid sodium coolant, breeds more Pu-239 and U-233 from Thorium-232 blanket), Stage 3: Advanced Heavy Water Reactors (AHWRs - Thorium-232 and Uranium-233 fuel cycle); Small Modular Reactors (SMRs - up to 300 MWe capacity, factory-fabricated, passive safety systems); Nuclear Fusion (ITER - International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in Cadarache France, tokamak magnetic confinement, India supplying cryostat and cooling water systems)

Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEVs): Hydrogen fuel cell combines hydrogen stored in pressurized 700-bar tanks with atmospheric oxygen over platinum catalyst to produce electricity, emitting only pure water vapor ($2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + 	ext{Electricity}$); Higher driving range and faster 5-minute refuelling than battery EVs

ScienceTech.topic: Defence Technology: Missiles, Drones, Submarines & Radar
ScienceTech.keywords: Ramjet vs Scramjet engines, Hypersonic glide vehicles, Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) for submarines, S-400 system

sub_items.text: Missile Classification & Technology: Ballistic Missiles (rocket-propelled into upper atmosphere/space, follow elliptical parabolic trajectory governed by gravity and drag, unguided in terminal phase, long-range; Agni series: Agni-P, Agni-V ICBM with >5000 km range, MIRV - Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicles tested in Mission Divyastra) vs Cruise Missiles (aerodynamically propelled by jet engine, fly inside atmosphere at low altitudes hugging terrain, continuously guided; BrahMos supersonic cruise missile Mach 2.8-3.0 developed with Russia, Nirbhay subsonic cruise missile)

Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP): Conceived by Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam in 1983; 5 core missiles (Mnemonic PATNA): Prithvi (surface-to-surface short range), Agni (surface-to-surface intermediate to intercontinental), Trishul (surface-to-air quick reaction), Nag (third-generation anti-tank fire-and-forget missile, Helina air-launched variant, MPATGM), Akash (medium-range surface-to-air missile, Rajendra phased-array radar)

Air Defence Systems & Radars: S-400 Triumf (Russian long-range surface-to-air missile system, 4 missile types covering 40 km to 400 km); Project Kusha (indigenous long-range surface-to-air missile system / LRSAM being developed by DRDO); Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) Programme: Phase 1 (Prithvi Air Defence PAD for exo-atmospheric interception 50-80 km + Advanced Air Defence AAD / Ashwin for endo-atmospheric interception 15-30 km); Very Short Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS); Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) Radars (Uttam AESA radar)

Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) & Drone Tech: Drone Rules 2021 (liberalized airspace maps on DigitalSky platform: Green zone no permission, Yellow zone regulated, Red zone no-fly); Types: Nano (<250 g), Micro (250 g - 2 kg), Small (2-25 kg), Medium (25-150 kg), Large (>150 kg); Military UAVs: Heron Mark II, MQ-9B Predator / SeaGuardian (HALE - High Altitude Long Endurance from USA), Tapas-BH-201 (MALE - Medium Altitude Long Endurance developed by DRDO), Kamikaze / Loitering munitions; Anti-drone systems (D4 counter-drone system soft kill RF jamming + hard kill laser)

Naval Platforms & Submarine Technology: Aircraft Carriers: INS Vikramaditya (modified Kiev-class from Russia, STOBAR ski-jump take-off with arrestor recovery) & INS Vikrant (first indigenous aircraft carrier built by Cochin Shipyard); Project 75 Scorpene-class conventional diesel-electric submarines (INS Kalvari, Khanderi, Karanj, Vela, Vagir, Vagsheer built at Mazagon Dock with French Naval Group); Air Independent Propulsion (AIP - DRDO fuel cell AIP allows conventional submarines to stay submerged for 2-3 weeks without snorting); Nuclear Submarines (SSBN ballistic missile nuclear submarines: INS Arihant and INS Arighat completing India's nuclear triad; SSN nuclear attack submarines)

Fighter Aircraft & Stealth Technology: LCA Tejas (indigenous light combat aircraft, 4.5 generation, fly-by-wire, delta wing, manufactured by HAL; Tejas Mk-1A with AESA radar and Astra BVR missile); AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft - 5th generation stealth fighter programme with internal weapon bays, radar absorbent material, supercruise); Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV - scramjet engine operating at Mach 6+)

HistoryCulture.topic: Buddhism & Jainism: Philosophy, Councils, Literature & Art
HistoryCulture.keywords: Bodhisattvas (Avalokiteshvara, Maitreya), Hinayana vs Mahayana vs Vajrayana, Jain Syadvada & Anekantavada, Triratna

sub_items.text: Buddhism Philosophy & Doctrines: Four Noble Truths (Arya Satya: Dukkha, Samudaya, Nirodha, Magga / Eightfold Path Ashtangika Marga); Pratityasamutpada (Dependent Origination - cause and effect wheel of 12 nidanas); Anatta (No permanent self/soul) & Anicca (Impermanence); Nirvana as cessation of desire and rebirth; Middle Path (Madhyama Pratipada avoiding extreme asceticism and sensory indulgence)

Buddhist Councils: 1st Council (Rajagriha, 483 BC, King Ajatashatru, Chairman Mahakassapa, compiled Sutta Pitaka by Ananda & Vinaya Pitaka by Upali); 2nd Council (Vaishali, 383 BC, King Kalashoka, Sabakami, split into Sthaviravadins & Mahasanghikas); 3rd Council (Pataliputra, 250 BC, King Ashoka, Moggaliputta Tissa, compiled Abhidhamma Pitaka, sent missionaries abroad); 4th Council (Kundalvana Kashmir, 72 AD, King Kanishka, Vasumitra & Ashvaghosha, final split into Hinayana and Mahayana)

Buddhist Literature: Tipitaka in Pali: Vinaya Pitaka (monastic discipline rules: Suttavibhanga, Khandhaka, Parivara), Sutta Pitaka (Buddha's discourses: 5 Nikayas including Digha, Majjhima, Samyutta, Anguttara, Khuddaka containing Jataka tales and Dhammapada), Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical analysis, Kathavatthu); Non-canonical texts: Milindapanho (questions of Indo-Greek king Menander to monk Nagasena), Visuddhimagga (by Buddhaghosa), Mahavamsa & Dipavamsa (Sri Lankan chronicles)

Buddhist Schools: Theravada / Hinayana (orthodox, Pali language, Buddha as human teacher, Arhat ideal of individual salvation) vs Mahayana (Sanskrit, Buddha deified, Bodhisattva ideal deferring own nirvana to save all beings: Avalokiteshvara/Padmapani compassion, Manjushri wisdom, Maitreya future Buddha, Vajrapani power) vs Vajrayana / Tantric Buddhism (Mantras, Dharanis, Mandalas, Tara goddess, Vikramashila university patronized by Palas); Madhyamaka (Nagarjuna - Shunyata/emptiness doctrine) vs Yogacara (Asanga & Vasubandhu - mind only / Vijnanavada)

Jainism Doctrines: Tirthankaras (24 Tirthankaras: Rishabhanatha 1st, Parshvanatha 23rd who gave 4 vows, Vardhamana Mahavira 24th who added Brahmacharya/celibacy); 5 Mahavratas (Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha, Brahmacharya); Anekantavada (doctrine of manifold nature of reality / non-absolutism) & Syadvada (theory of conditioned predication / 7-fold judgements); Triratna (Right Faith Samyak Darshana, Right Knowledge Samyak Jnana, Right Conduct Samyak Charitra); Believes soul (Jiva) exists even in stones, water, wind; Karma as physical matter binding soul; Sallekhana / Santhara (voluntary fasting unto death, Chandragupta Maurya at Shravanabelagola)

Jain Sects & Councils: Digambaras (Sky-clad / naked, led by Bhadrabahu who migrated south to Shravanabelagola during Magadha famine, believe women cannot attain liberation without rebirth as man) vs Shvetambaras (White-clad, led by Sthulabhadra who stayed in Magadha, acknowledge 19th Tirthankara Mallinatha as female); 1st Jain Council (Pataliputra, 300 BC, under Sthulabhadra, compiled 12 Angas); 2nd Jain Council (Vallabhi Gujarat, 512 AD, under Devardhi Kshamasramana, final compilation of Shvetambara Agamas in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit)

HistoryCulture.keywords: Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience (Salt March), Quit India Movement (Do or Die, parallel governments)

sub_items.text: Arrival of Gandhi & Early Local Experiments (1915–1918): Returned to India 9 Jan 1915 (Pravasi Bharatiya Divas) on Gokhale's advice; Champaran Satyagraha (1917, Bihar, First Civil Disobedience - against Tinkathia system forcing 3/20th land under indigo cultivation, joined by Rajendra Prasad, JB Kripalani); Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918, Gujarat, First Hunger Strike - dispute over Plague Bonus, demanded 35% wage hike, Anusuya Sarabhai); Kheda Satyagraha (1918, Gujarat, First Non-Cooperation - revenue remission demand due to crop failure under Revenue Code, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel joined)

Rowlatt Satyagraha & Jallianwala Bagh (1919): Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act 1919 - detention without trial for up to 2 years, habeas corpus suspended, no dalil no vakil no appeal); Satyagraha Sabha formed; Nationwide hartal 6 April 1919; Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar, General Dyer opened fire on peaceful gathering protesting arrest of Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr Satyapal); Rabindranath Tagore renounced Knighthood; Hunter Commission appointed; Congress appointed non-official inquiry committee (Motilal Nehru, Gandhi, CR Das)

Non-Cooperation & Khilafat Movement (NCM 1920–1922): Khilafat issue (preservation of Caliph's temporal authority in Ottoman Empire post-WWI, Ali Brothers: Shaukat Ali & Mohammad Ali, Abul Kalam Azad); Special Calcutta Congress (Sept 1920) approved NCM; Nagpur Congress (Dec 1920, CR Das moved resolution): Reorganized Congress on linguistic Provincial Congress Committees (PCCs), membership fee reduced to 4 annas, goal changed to Swaraj through peaceful means; Boycott of government schools, law courts, foreign cloth, titles surrendered (Gandhi returned Kaiser-i-Hind medal); Tilak Swaraj Fund oversubscribed; Chauri Chaura incident (4 Feb 1922, Gorakhpur UP - mob torched police station killing 22 policemen) $\rightarrow$ Gandhi abruptly withdrew NCM on 12 Feb 1922 (Bardoli resolution)

Swarajists vs No-Changers & Simon Commission (1922–1928): Swarajists (CR Das, Motilal Nehru - advocated entering legislative councils to 'wreck from within') vs No-Changers (Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, C Rajagopalachari - advocated constructive rural work, spinning, anti-untouchability); Simon Commission (1927 - all-white 7-member Indian Statutory Commission to review 1919 Act, boycotted by Congress and Muslim League; Lala Lajpat Rai succumbed to lathi charge injuries in Lahore); Nehru Report (1928 - drafted by Motilal Nehru committee: Dominion Status, Fundamental Rights, Universal Adult Suffrage, joint electorates with reservation for minorities, rejected by Jinnah who gave 14 Points)

Civil Disobedience Movement (CDM 1930–1934): Lahore Congress (Dec 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru president): Passed Purna Swaraj resolution, tri-colour unfurled on Ravi bank, 26 Jan 1930 declared Independence Day; Gandhi's 11 Demands to Viceroy Irwin; Dandi March (12 March to 6 April 1930, 78 ashram inmates marched 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi, broke salt law); Regional spread: C Rajagopalachari (Vedaranyam Salt March in TN), K Kelappan (Vaikom to Payyanur in Malabar), Sarojini Naidu & Manilal Gandhi (Dharasana Salt Works raid, brutally beaten, reported by Webb Miller), Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan / Frontier Gandhi (Khudai Khidmatgars / Red Shirts in NWFP), Rani Gaidinliu (Naga movement); First Round Table Conference (1930 - Congress boycotted); Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931 - suspension of CDM, release of political prisoners not guilty of violence, right to make salt for personal use); Karachi Congress (March 1931, Patel president): Resolutions on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme (drafted by Nehru); Second RTC (1931 - Gandhi attended as sole Congress representative, deadlocked on minority electorates); Resumption of CDM and brutal suppression; Communal Award (1932 by Ramsay MacDonald - separate electorates for Depressed Classes) $\rightarrow$ Gandhi's fast unto death in Yerwada Jail $\rightarrow$ Poona Pact (Sept 1932 between Gandhi and BR Ambedkar: abandoned separate electorates, increased reserved seats in provincial legislatures from 71 to 147)

Quit India Movement (1942) & August Revolution: Cripps Mission (March 1942 - promised Dominion Status post-WWII, Constituent Assembly, right of provinces to secede; rejected by Gandhi as 'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'); All-India Congress Committee meeting at Gowalia Tank Bombay (8 August 1942) passed Quit India Resolution: Gandhi's mantra 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro); Operation Zero Hour (midnight arrest of all top Congress leadership); Leaderless spontaneous mass uprising; Underground networks: Aruna Asaf Ali unfurled flag, Usha Mehta operated secret Congress Radio in Bombay, Jayaprakash Narayan and Rammanohar Lohia organized Azad Dasta; Parallel Governments (Prati Sarkar): Ballia (UP under Chittu Pandey), Tamluk / Jatiya Sarkar (Midnapore Bengal under Satish Samanta, Vidyut Vahini), Satara (Maharashtra under Nana Patil and YB Chavan - lasted till 1945); British deployed extreme force, machine-gunning from air

HistoryCulture.keywords: Morley-Minto (Separate Electorates), Montagu-Chelmsford (Dyarchy in Provinces), GoI Act 1935 (Provincial Autonomy, Federal Court)

sub_items.text: Government of India Act 1858 & Indian Councils Act 1861: Act of 1858 (Act for the Better Government of India post-1857 revolt, abolished East India Company rule and Board of Control/Court of Directors, transferred power to British Crown; created Secretary of State for India assisted by 15-member Council of India; Governor-General designated Viceroy, Lord Canning first Viceroy); Indian Councils Act 1861 (initiated decentralization, restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras, introduced portfolio system; empowered Viceroy to issue ordinances during emergency with 6 months validity; non-official Indian members nominated: Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao)

Indian Councils Act 1892 & Morley-Minto Reforms 1909: Act of 1892 (introduced indirect election / nomination for non-official members, allowed legislative councils to discuss budget and address questions to executive, but NO supplementary questions or voting on budget); Morley-Minto Reforms / Indian Councils Act 1909 (introduced SEPARATE ELECTORATES for Muslims - Lord Minto known as 'Father of Communal Electorate'; allowed members to move resolutions and ask supplementary questions on budget; first Indian appointed to Viceroy's Executive Council: Satyendra Prasad Sinha as Law Member)

Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms): Introduced DYARCHY in Provinces (Divided provincial subjects into 'Transferred' administered by Governor on advice of elected Ministers responsible to legislature e.g. education, health, agriculture, and 'Reserved' administered by Governor and Executive Council without legislative accountability e.g. police, justice, land revenue, finance); Introduced BICAMERALISM at Centre (Council of State and Central Legislative Assembly); Introduced direct elections with limited franchise based on property, tax, education (~10% population); Extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans; Created office of High Commissioner for India in London; Provided for establishment of Public Service Commission (Central PSC set up in 1926 on Lee Commission recommendation); Separated provincial budgets from central budget

Simon Commission Recommendations & Round Table Conferences (1927–1932): Simon Report (1930 recommended abolition of provincial dyarchy, introduction of responsible government in provinces, retention of communal electorates till communal consensus, rejection of central dyarchy); 3 Round Table Conferences in London; White Paper on Constitutional Reforms (1933) examined by Joint Select Committee chaired by Lord Linlithgow $\rightarrow$ drafted Government of India Act 1935

Government of India Act 1935: Detailed, lengthy legislation (321 sections, 10 schedules); Proposed All-India Federation comprising British Indian provinces and princely states (never came into being because princely states refused to join); Abolished Dyarchy in Provinces and introduced PROVINCIAL AUTONOMY (responsible government with ministers accountable to elected legislatures); Introduced DYARCHY at Centre (Federal subjects divided into Reserved: defence, external affairs, tribal affairs, ecclesiastical administered by Governor-General, and Transferred); Divided powers into 3 Lists: Federal List (59 items), Provincial List (54 items), Concurrent List (36 items); Residuary powers vested in GOVERNOR-GENERAL (not legislature); Introduced bicameralism in 6 out of 11 provinces (Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, UP); Established Federal Court (1937, Sir Maurice Gwyer first Chief Justice), Reserve Bank of India (1935), Federal Public Service Commission and Joint PSC; Extended communal representation to Depressed Classes (Scheduled Castes), women, and labor; Abolished Council of India of Secretary of State; Retained communal electorates and British veto powers

Wavell Plan (1945), Cabinet Mission (1946) & Indian Independence Act 1947: Wavell Plan / Shimla Conference (1945 - reconstruct Viceroy's Executive Council with all Indian members except Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief, equal representation to Caste Hindus and Muslims, failed due to Jinnah's insistence that Muslim League alone nominate Muslim members); Cabinet Mission Plan (1946 - Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, AV Alexander: Rejected separate Pakistan, proposed loose three-tier Indian Union with Centre controlling defence, foreign affairs, communications; Grouping of provinces into Section A Hindu-majority, Section B Muslim-majority northwest, Section C Muslim-majority northeast; Constituent Assembly to frame constitution); Mountbatten Plan / 3 June Plan (1947 - partition of India and transfer of power on 15 August 1947; boundary commission under Sir Cyril Radcliffe); Indian Independence Act 1947 (passed by British Parliament on 18 July 1947: created two independent dominions India and Pakistan, abolished office of Viceroy and Secretary of State, empowered Constituent Assemblies of both dominions to frame any constitution and repeal any British act including 1947 Act itself; designated Governor-General as constitutional nominal head till new constitution enacted)

HistoryCulture.topic: Temple Architecture & Sculptural Traditions of India
HistoryCulture.keywords: Nagara vs Dravida vs Vesara, Shikhara/Vimana, Mandapa, Panchayatan style, Chola bronzes (Nataraja), Ajanta/Ellora caves

sub_items.text: Temple Architecture Styles & Evolution: Nagara (North Indian style, square sanctum Garbhagriha, curvilinear Shikhara / Rekhaprasada, Amalaka stone disc with Kalasha finial at top, temple built on raised plinth / Jagati, NO boundary walls or elaborate gateways) vs Dravida (South Indian style, stepped pyramidical tower Vimana crowned by octagonal Shikhara, enclosed within high boundary walls, monumental entrance gateways GOPURAMS, presence of large temple water tank Kalyani inside complex, pillared assembly halls Mandapas) vs Vesara / Hybrid style (Karnataka style under Chalukyas and Hoysalas blending Nagara shikhara with Dravida vimana layout, star-shaped / stellate ground plan)

Sub-Schools of Nagara Architecture: Odisha School (Kalinga style: Deula tower - Rekhadeula sanctum, Pidhadula assembly hall Jagamohana, Khakharadeula; Jagannath Puri, Lingaraja at Bhubaneswar, Sun Temple Konark / Black Pagoda designed as giant chariot with 24 carved stone wheels pulled by 7 horses); Khajuraho School (Chandela rulers in Bundelkhand, temples on high platforms, subsidiary shrines in Panchayatana style, interconnected halls Ardhamandapa-Mandapa-Mahamandapa-Antarala-Garbhagriha, erotic Mithuna sculptures and spiritual figures, Kandariya Mahadeva temple, Lakshmana temple); Solanki / Maru-Gurjara School (Gujarat and Rajasthan under Solankis, stepwells Kund adjacent to temple, intricate carved marble ceilings; Modhera Sun Temple with Surya Kund stepped water tank, Dilwara Jain Temples at Mount Abu carved in white marble)

Evolution of Dravidian Architecture: Pallava Phase (Rock-cut cave temples Mandapas under Mahendravarman I $\rightarrow$ Monolithic rock-cut shrines Rathas / Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram under Narasimhavarman I Mamalla: Dharmaraja ratha, Arjuna ratha, Draupadi ratha $\rightarrow$ Structural stone temples under Rajasimha: Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, Kailasanathar Temple at Kanchipuram) $\rightarrow$ Chola Phase (Grand structural Dravida monuments: Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur / Rajarajesvaram built by Rajaraja I in 1010 AD, 66m high Vimana with single 80-tonne granite octagonal capstone, fresco murals, bronze Nataraja; Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikondacholapuram built by Rajendra I; Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram by Rajaraja II) $\rightarrow$ Vijayanagara Phase (Raya Gopurams, Kalyana Mandapam with elaborately carved musical pillars depicting Yali mythical beasts, Amman shrine for consort; Virupaksha Temple and Vittala Temple at Hampi with stone chariot) $\rightarrow$ Nayaka Phase (Madurai Meenakshi Temple, enormous 1000-pillared mandapas, tallest gopurams, concentric prakaras)

Vesara & Hoysala Architecture: Badami Chalukyas (Aihole cradle of Indian temple architecture: Lad Khan temple, Durga temple with apsidal plan resembling Buddhist chaitya; Badami rock-cut cave temples; Pattadakal UNESCO site with both Nagara Papanatha and Dravida Virupaksha temples); Rashtrakutas (Kailasanatha Temple at Cave 16 Ellora - world's largest monolithic rock-cut monument carved top-down from single basalt cliff under Krishna I in 8th century AD); Hoysalas of Belur, Halebidu and Somnathpura (Chennakeshava Temple Belur, Hoysaleswara Temple Halebidu, Keshava Temple Somnathpura: carved out of soft chloritic schist / soapstone, stellate star-shaped platforms, horizontal friezes depicting elephants, lions, cavalry, mythical makaras, celestial dancers Madanikas)

Rock-Cut Architecture: Buddhist Caves: Ajanta Caves (Aurangabad Maharashtra, 29 caves, 2nd century BC to 6th century AD, Hinayana and Mahayana phases, Viharas monastery living quarters and Chaityas apsidal prayer halls with stupa; famous fresco murals depicting Jataka tales, Bodhisattva Padmapani and Vajrapani, dying princess, narrative perspective) & Ellora Caves (34 caves: Caves 1-12 Buddhist, Caves 13-29 Hindu including monolithic Kailash temple Cave 16, Caves 30-34 Jain including Indra Sabha; carved out of basaltic trap, multi-storeyed); Elephanta Caves (Mumbai harbour, Shaivite rock-cut sculptures, 6-meter colossal trimurti Maheshamurti representing Creator, Preserver, Destroyer aspects); Barabar Caves (Bihar, oldest surviving rock-cut caves, Mauryan period, dedicated by Ashoka and Dasaratha to Ajivika ascetic sect; Lomas Rishi cave with polished granite interior and horseshoe carved facade)

Sculptural Traditions: Harappan Bronze Casting (Lost-wax / cire perdue method: Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro, bronze buffalo); Gandhara School of Art (1st to 5th century AD, Greco-Roman influence, blue-grey schist sandstone, Buddha with wavy Greek hair, Apollo-like facial features, heavy realistic drapery, moustache, protuberant ushnisha topknot, urna forehead mark) vs Mathura School of Art (indigenous development, spotted red sandstone, Buddha with smiling round face, shaven head, tight transparent drapery, broad shoulders, massive masculine physique, accompanied by Yakshas and Bodhisattvas) vs Sarnath School of Art (Gupta classical golden age, Chunar sandstone, serene meditative spiritual calm, spiritual glow prabhamandala halo with floral carvings, transparent drapery without folds, Dharmachakra Pravartana Mudra Buddha); Chola Bronzes (Lost-wax bronze casting peak; Nataraja cosmic dance: Anandatandava pose, right foot crushing demon Apasmara ignorance, upper right hand holding Damaru drum creation, upper left hand holding Agni flame destruction, lower right hand in Abhaya mudra fearlessness, lower left hand pointing to lifted foot refuge, ring of cosmic flames Tiruvasi)

sub_items.text: Origin & Dynasties of Vijayanagara (1336–1646): Founded in 1336 on southern banks of Tungabhadra river by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of Sangama Dynasty, inspired by sage Vidyaranya; 4 Dynasties: Sangama (1336–1485) $\rightarrow$ Saluva (1485–1505, founded by Saluva Narasimha) $\rightarrow$ Tuluva (1505–1570, founded by Vira Narasimha, zenith under Krishnadeva Raya) $\rightarrow$ Aravidu (1570–1646, founded by Tirumala post-Talikota, shifted capital to Penukonda and Chandragiri)

Krishnadeva Raya (reigned 1509–1529): Greatest ruler of Tuluva dynasty; Military conquests: Defeated Sultan of Bijapur, captured Raichur Doab (1520), defeated Gajapati ruler of Odisha Prataparudra and married his daughter, captured Udayagiri and Kondavidu forts; Titles: Andhra Bhoja, Mooru Rayara Ganda, Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya (restorer of Yavana kingdom); Literary patronage: Astadiggajas (8 great Telugu poets in his court, prominent among them Allasani Peddana author of Manucharitam, Tenali Ramakrishna author of Panduranga Mahatmyam); Author of Amuktamalyada (Telugu political treatise on statecraft and administrative duties of a king) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit play); Built new township Nagalapuram near Vijayanagara in memory of his mother Nagala Devi, commissioned Raya Gopurams across South India

Administration & Nayankara System: Central administration headed by King assisted by Council of Ministers; Empire divided into administrative tiers: Rajya / Mandala (governed by royal prince or noble) $\rightarrow$ Vishaya / Nadu (district) $\rightarrow$ Sthala / Seema (sub-district) $\rightarrow$ Grama (village); Ayagar System in villages: 12 village functionaries (Karnam/accountant, Talayari/watchman, blacksmith, potter, etc.) granted tax-free land (Manyam) in return for hereditary public services; Nayankara / Amara-Nayaka System: Military commanders (Amara-Nayakas) assigned territories (Amara / Nayakkattanam) by king; collected taxes, maintained fixed contingent of elephants, cavalry and foot soldiers for king's military campaigns, paid annual tribute to royal treasury; Fernao Nuniz and Domingo Paes recorded that nayakas retained high revenue and kept king informed through representatives at capital

Foreign Travellers to Vijayanagara: Nicolo de Conti (Italian, visited in 1420 during Devaraya I, described city circumference, festivals like Deepavali and Mahanavami); Abdur Razzak (Persian ambassador sent by Timurid ruler Shahrukh, visited 1443 during Devaraya II, recorded 7 concentric fortified city walls enclosing agricultural fields and orchards, described mint and brothels); Duarte Barbosa (Portuguese, visited 1500-1516, detailed trade in diamonds, horses and textiles); Domingo Paes (Portuguese, visited 1520-1522 during Krishnadeva Raya, called Vijayanagara as large as Rome with beautiful palaces, praised Krishnadeva Raya's appearance and justice); Fernao Nuniz (Portuguese horse-trader, visited 1535-1537 during Achyuta Deva Raya, detailed chronicle of dynasties and women employees in palace: astrologers, wrestlers, accountants, security guards); Cesare Federici (Italian, visited 1567 post-Talikota, recorded city completely destroyed and depopulated)

Economic Life & Hampi Architecture: Thriving international trade: Imported Arabian and Persian warhorses via Portuguese Goa (trade monopoly protected by Krishnadeva Raya), silk from China, spices from Maluku; Exported textiles, rice, iron, spices, precious stones (Golconda diamond mines); Coinage: Gold coins called Varaha / Pagoda bearing images of Hindu deities (Venkateshwara, Shiva-Parvati) and bull/elephant emblems; Architecture at Hampi (UNESCO World Heritage Site): Urban core, Royal Enclosure, Sacred Centre; Mahanavami Dibba (massive 11-meter high stone platform carved with military processions, hunting scenes, where king witnessed Mahanavami/Dussehra festival and reviewed armies); Queens Bath, Lotus Mahal (Indo-Islamic secular architecture with vaulted ceilings and arches), Elephant Stables (11 domed chambers for royal elephants), Stepped Tank (Pushkarani carved in chlorite schist with geometric symmetry)

Battle of Talikota / Rakkasa-Tangadi (1565) & Decline: Constant conflict over fertile Raichur Doab (between Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers) and Krishna-Godavari delta with Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar, Berar); Regent Aliya Rama Raya played one Sultanate against another; 4 Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar - Berar excluded) formed grand military coalition; Battle fought on 23 January 1565 at Rakkasa-Tangadi / Talikota: Vijayanagara army routed, Rama Raya captured and beheaded by Husain Nizam Shah; Victorious Sultanate armies sacked, burned and looted magnificent metropolis of Vijayanagara for 6 months, reducing it to ruins; Capital shifted to Penukonda by Rama Raya's brother Tirumala Raya who established Aravidu dynasty

sub_items.text: Mauryan Empire Origin & Expansion: Founded in 321 BC by Chandragupta Maurya with assistance of Chanakya / Kautilya / Vishnugupta, overthrowing Dhanananda (last Nanda ruler of Magadha); Defeated Seleucus Nicator (Alexander's general, 305 BC) securing Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Baluchistan), Paropamisadae (Kabul), and Aria (Herat); Megasthenes sent as Greek ambassador to Pataliputra; Bindusara (Amitraghata / slayer of foes, 297–273 BC, patronized Ajivika sect, requested sweet wine, dried figs, and a sophist from Antiochus I of Syria); Ashoka the Great (268–232 BC, Kalinga War 261 BC described in Major Rock Edict XIII caused profound remorse, renounced Bherighosha / conquest by war and adopted Dhammaghosha / conquest by righteousness)

Kautilya's Arthashastra & Saptanga Theory: Masterwork on statecraft, economic policy and military strategy in Sanskrit prose and verse (rediscovered by R. Shamasastry in 1905); Saptanga Theory (7 Limbs of the State): 1. Swami (The Sovereign King / Head), 2. Amatya (Ministers and officials / Eyes), 3. Janapada / Rashtra (Territory and population / Legs), 4. Durga (Fortified capital / Arms), 5. Kosha (Treasury / Mouth), 6. Danda / Bala (Army and military strength / Brain), 7. Mitra (Allies and friends / Ears); Mandala Theory of geopolitical foreign relations (Raja-mandala: 12 kings in circle of diplomacy, immediate neighbour is natural enemy Ari, neighbour's neighbour is natural friend Mitra); Elaborate espionage system (Sanstha stationary spies & Sanchara wandering spies, Vishakanyas)

Megasthenes' Indica & Mauryan Administration: Fragments preserved in writings of Strabo, Arrian, Diodorus; Described Pataliputra as palisaded city at confluence of Ganga and Son, 64 gates and 570 towers; City Administration (Nagarak) governed by 6 municipal boards of 5 members each: 1. Industrial arts, 2. Care of foreigners, 3. Registration of births and deaths, 4. Trade and commerce/weights, 5. Inspection of manufactured goods, 6. Collection of 1/10th sales tax; Military Administration overseen by 6 boards of 5 members: Infantry, Cavalry, War Elephants, Chariots, Navy, Transport and logistics; Megasthenes' 7 Castes in Indian society: Philosophers, Farmers (largest class), Herdsmen/Hunters, Artisans/Traders, Warriors, Overseers/Inspectors, Councillors/Assessors; Remarked (erroneously) that slavery did NOT exist in India and Indians never had famines

Ashokan Edicts & Decipherment: Deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837; Inscriptions refer to Ashoka as Devanampiya Piyadassi ('Beloved of the Gods, of Gracious Mien'); Name 'Ashoka' explicitly mentioned in only 4 minor edicts: Maski (Karnataka), Gurjarra (MP), Nittur, and Udegolam (Karnataka); Written in Prakrit language using Brahmi script across most of India, Kharosthi script in North-West (Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra written right-to-left), Greek and Aramaic bilingual scripts in Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna)

Major Rock Edicts & Ashoka's Dhamma: 14 Major Rock Edicts: Edict I (Prohibition of animal sacrifice and festive gatherings), Edict II (Medical facilities for humans and animals, planting medicinal herbs along roads in Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputra, Keralaputra, Tamraparni/Sri Lanka), Edict III (Generosity to Brahmanas and Shramanas, Yuktas, Rajukas, Pradesikas tour every 5 years), Edict V (Appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas in 13th regnal year), Edict VIII (Royal pleasure tours Viharayatra replaced by Dhamma tours Dhammayatra; visit to Bodh Gaya), Edict XII (Religious tolerance and respect for all sects, essence of religion Saravriddhi), Edict XIII (Horrors of Kalinga War, conquest by Dhamma superior to conquest by sword, mentions 5 contemporary Hellenistic Greek kings: Antiochus II of Syria, Ptolemy II Philadelphus of Egypt, Antigonus Gonatas of Macedonia, Magas of Cyrene, Alexander of Epirus); Pillar Edicts (7 Pillar Edicts: Delhi-Topra, Delhi-Meerut brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq, Lauriya-Nandangarh, Lauriya-Araraj, Rampurva, Allahabad-Kosam); Rummindei / Lumbini Pillar Edict (records Ashoka's personal pilgrimage to Buddha's birthplace, exempted Lumbini from religious tax Bali and reduced land revenue Bhaga from 1/6th to 1/8th)

Mauryan Art & Architecture: Royal Court Art patronized by state vs Popular Folk Art: Monolithic Pillars (Chunar sandstone, mirror-like lustrous polish, tapering cylindrical shaft, inverted lotus bell capital, abacus frieze, crowning animal sculpture: Sarnath Lion Capital adopted as National Emblem of India with 4 Asiatic lions seated back-to-back, abacus carved with Elephant, Galloping Horse, Bull, Lion separated by 24-spoke Dharmachakra wheels; Rampurva Bull Capital; Lauriya-Nandangarh Lion); Stupas (Sanchi Stupa 1 core built by Ashoka, Anda hemispherical dome, Harmika square railing, Chhatri triple umbrella, Torana gateways added later by Satavahanas); Yaksha and Yakshini Stone Sculptures (Didarganj Yakshini carrying fly-whisk chauri, polished sandstone masterpiece of popular art; Parkham Yaksha)

HistoryCulture.topic: Bhakti & Sufi Movements: Saints, Philosophy & Literature
HistoryCulture.keywords: Saguna vs Nirguna, Kabir, Guru Nanak, Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita), Shankaradeva, Chisti vs Suhrawardi silsilas

sub_items.text: Origin & Philosophy of Bhakti Movement: Emerged in 7th–9th century South India with Alvar (Vaishnavite, 12 saints including Nammalvar, Periyalvar, and only female saint Andal, compiled Nalayira Divya Prabandham / Tamil Veda) and Nayanar (Shaivite, 63 saints including Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, Manikkavacakar, compiled Tevaram and Tiruvacakam); Rejected Vedic ritualism, caste distinctions, monopoly of Sanskrit, preached loving devotion (Bhakti) directly to personal God in local vernacular languages; Northern spread in 14th–17th centuries under Ramananda ('Bhakti dravida upaji, laye Ramananda')

Saguna vs Nirguna Bhakti Traditions: Saguna Bhakti (devotion to God WITH form, attributes, human incarnations / Avatars of Vishnu or Shiva: Ramanuja, Madhvacharya, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Vallabhacharya, Surdas, Tulsidas, Mirabai, Shankaradeva) vs Nirguna Bhakti (devotion to formless, attribute-less, omnipresent Supreme Being / Satguru, rejected idol worship, pilgrimages, scriptures: Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal, Raidas/Ravidas)

Key Bhakti Saints & Literature: Adi Shankaracharya (8th century, Advaita Vedanta non-dualism: Brahman alone is real, world is Maya/illusion, established 4 Mathas at Sringeri, Puri, Dwarka, Badrinath); Ramanujacharya (11th century, Vishishtadvaita qualified non-dualism: soul and matter are real attributes of Brahman/Vishnu, propounded Prapatti / surrender, Statue of Equality at Hyderabad); Madhvacharya (13th century, Dvaita dualism: eternal distinction between God, individual souls, and matter); Kabir (15th century weaver of Varanasi, disciple of Ramananda, syncretic Nirguna saint, attacked orthodoxy of both Hinduism and Islam, compositions in Panchmel Khichdi / Sadhukkadi dialect: Bijak containing Sakhis, Sabads, Ramainis, included in Guru Granth Sahib); Guru Nanak (1469–1539, founder of Sikhism, Nirguna devotion to Ik Onkar, started community kitchen Langar and Sangat, rejected caste hierarchy; succession of 10 Gurus compiled Adi Granth by Guru Arjan Dev in 1604); Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi dialect, Vinaya Patrika, Kavitavali); Surdas (Sur Sagar, Sur Saravali in Braj Bhasha Krishna bhakti); Mirabai (devotional Padas to Giridhar Gopal in Rajasthani and Braj); Shankaradeva (15th-16th century Assam, founded Ekasarana Dharma, Neo-Vaishnavite movement, created Satras monasteries and Namghars prayer houses, developed Sattriya classical dance, Borgeet songs, Ankiya Naat drama)

Maharashtra Dharma / Varkari & Dharakari Sects: Pandharpur pilgrimage movement centered on Vithoba / Vitthala (manifestation of Krishna) and his consort Rakhumai on banks of Bhima/Chandrabhaga river; Jnaneshwar / Dnyaneshwar (13th century, wrote Bhavartha Dipika / Dnyaneshwari - Marathi commentary on Bhagavad Gita); Namdev (tailor, travelled to Punjab, 61 of his hymns included in Guru Granth Sahib); Eknath (wrote Eknathi Bhagavata, promoted vernacular Abhangas); Tukaram (17th century Shudra grocer, contemporary of Shivaji, master of devotional Abhang poetry, preached egalitarian spiritual fellowship); Ramdas (Dharakari martial tradition, spiritual preceptor of Chhatrapati Shivaji, author of Dasbodh)

Sufism Origin, Principles & Concepts: Mystical reform movement in Islam originating in Persia; Emphasized direct experiential love and communion with God (Ishq-e-Haqiqi), asceticism, inner purification (Tazkiya); Key Concepts: Murid (disciple) guides under Pir / Murshid / Shaikh (spiritual preceptor); Khanqah (hospice / monastery where Sufi saints lived and held spiritual assemblies); Silsilah (spiritual lineage / chain connecting disciple back to Prophet Muhammad); Sama (musical spiritual gatherings to induce mystical ecstasy / Wajd); Fana (annihilation of ego in divine love) $\rightarrow$ Baqa (subsistence in divine consciousness); Ziyarat (pilgrimage to Sufi shrines / Dargahs on death anniversary / Urs / union with God)

Major Sufi Silsilahs in India: Chishti Silsilah (founded in India by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in 1192 at Ajmer; embraced poverty, strictly avoided state patronage and royal court politics, open kitchen Langar, welcomed music Sama; notable saints: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki after whom Qutb Minar is named, Baba Farid / Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar whose verses appear in Guru Granth Sahib, Nizamuddin Auliya / Mehboob-e-Ilahi of Delhi who witnessed 7 sultans, Amir Khusro poet, Nasiruddin Chirag-i-Dehlavi) vs Suhrawardi Silsilah (founded in India by Bahauddin Zakariya at Multan; accepted state offices, land grants, royal patronage from Delhi Sultans, argued saint must have wealth to help poor) vs Qadiri Silsilah (popularized in Punjab and Sindh, Dara Shikoh eldest son of Shah Jahan was ardent disciple of Mian Mir and Mulla Shah Badakhshi, authored Majma-ul-Bahrain / Mingling of Two Oceans comparing Sufism and Vedanta) vs Naqshbandi Silsilah (orthodox, revivalist, established by Khwaja Baqi Billah, prominent under Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani who fiercely opposed Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul, opposed music Sama, demanded strict adherence to Sharia, patronized by Aurangzeb)

HistoryCulture.topic: Indus Valley Civilization: Major Sites & Urban Planning
HistoryCulture.keywords: Dholavira (water harvesting reservoir, signboard), Lothal dockyard, Kalibangan ploughed field, absence of iron/horse proof

sub_items.text: Origin, Chronology & Extent of Harappan Civilization: Mature Harappan Phase dated ~2600–1900 BC using radiocarbon; Bronze Age civilization covering ~1.3 million sq km across north-western subcontinent; Geographical Extent: Northernmost site: Manda (Chenab river, Jammu & Kashmir) or Shortugai (trading outpost in Badakhshan Afghanistan for lapis lazuli); Southernmost site: Daimabad (Pravara river, Maharashtra - bronze chariot found); Westernmost site: Sutkagan Dor (Dasht river, Makran coast Pakistan near Iranian border); Easternmost site: Alamgirpur (Hindon river, Meerut UP)

Urban Town Planning & Citadel Architecture: Grid pattern layout (streets cutting at right angles / chessboard system); Divided into two distinct parts: Western Citadel / Upper Town (built on raised mud-brick platform, fortified, housed administrative public buildings, elite residences) and Eastern Lower Town (larger, residential quarters for common working population); Exception: Dholera is divided into THREE parts (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town) with massive stone fortifications and large ceremonial ground; Standardized burnt mud bricks with uniform ratio 4:2:1 (length : breadth : height) across all settlements from Gujarat to Punjab

Drainage System & Public Sanitation: Most advanced municipal sanitation of Bronze Age world; Household drains made of burnt bricks flowed from bathrooms into street drains; Street drains covered with removable limestone slabs or bricks for cleaning; Soak pits and manholes at regular intervals; Houses had central courtyards with surrounding rooms, private bathrooms, wells, and staircases indicating two-storeyed structures; Windows opened into side lanes, NOT main streets (dust/noise reduction)

Major Harappan Sites & Diagnostic Findings: Mohenjo-daro (Mound of the Dead, Sindh on Indus river: Great Bath with bitumen/gypsum water-tight lining, Great Granary, Assembly Hall, Collegiate building, Bronze Dancing Girl, Steatite Bearded Priest-King, Pashupati proto-Shiva seal); Harappa (Punjab Pakistan on Ravi river: 6 granaries in two rows, working floors with circular brick platforms for threshing grain, barracks for workmen, R-37 cemetery, red sandstone male torso); Lothal (Gulf of Khambhat Gujarat on Bhogava river: Tidal dockyard made of burnt bricks with sluice gate, rice husk evidence, fire altars, terracotta model of ship, bead-making factory, Persian Gulf seal, joint burial); Kalibangan (Rajasthan on dried Ghaggar river: Ploughed agricultural field showing furrow marks at right angles, fire altars in rows, camel bones, wooden furrow, absence of drainage in early phase); Chanhudaro (Sindh, only Harappan city WITHOUT a citadel: Bead-making factory, inkpot, footprint of dog chasing cat, lipsticks/cosmetics); Banawali (Haryana on Ghaggar: Radial streets layout, high quality barley, clay toy model of plough); Rakhigarhi (Hisar Haryana: Largest IVC site in Indian subcontinent, necropolis excavations, DNA study)

Economy, Agriculture & Maritime Trade: Agriculture: Cultivated wheat, barley, sesamum, mustard, dates, peas; Cotton cultivated first time in world (Greeks called it 'Sindon' derived from Sindh); Rice husks found at Lothal and Rangpur; Ploughed fields at Kalibangan; Animal Husbandry: Domesticated humped cattle (zebu), buffalo, sheep, goat, pig, elephant; Horse remains disputed (Surkotada jawbone/horse tooth); Craft Specialization: Bead-making (carnelian, agate, steatite, lapis lazuli), bronze casting, pottery (red pottery painted with black geometric and animal designs - Black-on-Red ware); External Trade: Mesopotamian cuneiform tablets mention trade with 'Meluhha' (Indus region) through intermediate stations 'Dilmun' (Bahrain) and 'Magan' (Oman coast); Harappan cubical chert weights following binary (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 where 16 was standard unit = 13.7g) and decimal systems

Society, Religion & Script: Secular urban society with merchant/administrative dominance; Religion (No grand temples or religious structures found except Great Bath): Pashupati Seal (seated yogic figure surrounded by 4 animals: Elephant, Tiger, Rhinoceros, Buffalo, and two Antelopes/deer under seat); Mother Goddess terracotta figurines (symbolizing fertility); Worship of Pipal tree (Ficus religiosa), humped bull, phallic symbols (Lingam and Yoni stones), amulets for protection against evil spirits; Burial practices: Extended inhumation (head to north), urn burials, fractional burials, grave goods (pottery, mirrors, shell ornaments indicating belief in afterlife); Harappan Script: Boustrophedon writing (written right-to-left in first line, left-to-right in second), pictographic / ideographic script with ~400 distinct signs, UN-DECIPHERED till date; Longest inscription found at Dholavira sign board (10 large Indus signs)

HistoryCulture.topic: Socio-Religious Reform Movements of the 19th Century
HistoryCulture.keywords: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj), Jyotirao Phule (Satyashodhak Samaj), Dayanand Saraswati (Arya Samaj), Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar

sub_items.text: Character & Nature of 19th Century Renaissance: Response to colonial critique of Indian society and Western modern scientific education; Dual approach: Reformist movements (advocated rationalism, humanism, elimination of social evils while adapting modern Western values: Brahmo Samaj, Prarthana Samaj, Aligarh Movement) vs Revivalist movements (advocated return to pristine ancient purity of scriptures, reviving indigenous glory while rejecting Western cultural superiority: Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna Mission, Deoband Movement); Addressed social evils: Sati, female infanticide, child marriage, polygamy, widow remarriage prohibition, caste untouchability, purdah system

Raja Ram Mohan Roy & Brahmo Samaj: 'Father of Indian Renaissance' / 'Maker of Modern India'; Established Atmiya Sabha (1814) to propagate monotheism and fight idolatry; Founded Brahmo Samaj (1828): Worship of one eternal unsearchable God, rejected idol worship, priesthood, animal sacrifice, incarnations, and sati; Authored 'Gift to Monotheists' (Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin in Persian 1809) and 'Precepts of Jesus' (1820 separating moral teachings from miracles); Relentless crusade led to Bengal Sati Regulation Act 1829 by Lord William Bentinck; Promoted modern education: Supported David Hare in founding Hindu College (1817), set up Vedanta College (1825); Journalistic pioneer: Published Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali weekly) and Mirat-ul-Akbar (Persian journal); Defended free press against Adams' Licensing Regulations 1823; Given title of 'Raja' by Mughal Emperor Akbar II

Schisms in Brahmo Samaj & Prarthana Samaj: Debendranath Tagore joined in 1842, founded Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) and journal Tattvabodhini Patrika for rational theological inquiry; Keshab Chandra Sen inducted (1858) dynamic radical reformer; 1st Schism (1866): Conservative faction under Debendranath formed 'Adi Brahmo Samaj' while Keshab formed 'Brahmo Samaj of India'; 2nd Schism (1878): Keshab married his underage 13-year-old daughter to Maharaja of Cooch Behar violating his own Native Marriage Act 1872 $\rightarrow$ Disgusted progressive followers (Anand Mohan Bose, Shibnath Shastri) broke away to form 'Sadharan Brahmo Samaj'; Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay): Founded by Atmaram Pandurang with help of Keshab Chandra Sen; Joined by Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade (built Indian National Social Conference 1887) and RG Bhandarkar; Focused on social reform: Inter-dining, inter-marriage, widow remarriage, upliftment of women and depressed classes; Avoided religious break with Hinduism

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar & Jyotirao Phule: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar: Principal of Sanskrit College Calcutta (opened college to non-Brahmin students), polymath, championed women's education (pioneered 35 girls' schools with JED Bethune); Crusade for widow remarriage citing Parashara Smriti led to Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856 passed by Lord Dalhousie/Canning; Jyotirao Phule (1827–1890, Maharashtra): Pioneer of anti-caste non-Brahmin movement; Founded Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) for social liberation of Shudras and Ati-Shudras; Established first girls' school at Bhide Wada Pune (1848) with his wife Savitribai Phule (first female teacher of India); Authored seminal polemical texts: Gulamgiri (Slavery 1873, dedicated to American movement against Black slavery) and Sarvajanik Satya Dharma; Replaced Brahmin priests with simple non-ritualistic wedding vows; Given title 'Mahatma' in 1888

Swami Dayanand Saraswati & Arya Samaj: Founded Arya Samaj in Bombay (1875), later headquarters shifted to Lahore; Slogan 'Go Back to the Vedas' (Vedas are infallible source of divine knowledge, rejected Puranas, idol worship, polytheism, child marriage, untouchability, hereditary caste); Propounded Shuddhi Movement (reconversion to Hinduism of those converted to Islam or Christianity); Authored Satyarth Prakash (The Light of Truth 1875); Introduced DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) college movement in Lahore (1886) under Lala Hansraj $\rightarrow$ Led to split in 1893 between College Party (moderate, favoured English education and vegetarianism non-strict) and Gurukul Party (Swami Shraddhanand who established Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar in 1902 emphasizing Vedic education and strict brahmacharya)

Swami Vivekananda, Theosophical Society & Islamic Reforms: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa (mystic priest of Dakshineswar Kali temple who realized truth of all religions); Swami Vivekananda (Narendranath Datta): Historic speech at Parliament of World's Religions Chicago (1893); Founded Ramakrishna Mission (1897) at Belur Math emphasizing Neo-Vedanta, practical spiritual humanism ('Service to Jiva is worship of Shiva'); Theosophical Society (founded in New York 1875 by Madam HP Blavatsky and Colonel HS Olcott, shifted HQ to Adyar Madras in 1882; popularized in India by Annie Besant who championed Hindu resurgence, established Central Hindu College Varanasi 1898 which became BHU); Islamic Reform Movements: Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan: Advocated modern scientific education for Muslims, founded Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875 which became AMU, published Tahdhib-ul-Akhlaq, opposed Congress politics) vs Deoband Movement (revivalist orthodox school founded in 1866 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi at Saharanpur UP; issued fatwa supporting Indian National Congress and opposing Syed Ahmad's loyalism)

HistoryCulture.keywords: Mansabdari system (Zat & Sawar), Jagirdari crisis, Todar Mal Bandobast (Zabti system), Dahsala system

sub_items.text: Mughal Administrative Structure: Centralized bureaucratic monarchy headed by Emperor (Zill-i-Ilahi / Shadow of God); Central Ministers: 1. Wazir / Diwan (Chief Minister in charge of finance and revenue), 2. Mir Bakshi (Head of military department, paymaster general, processed appointments and promotions of Mansabdars, maintained intelligence barids), 3. Mir Saman / Khan-i-Saman (Head of royal household, royal workshops / Karkhanas and stores), 4. Sadr-us-Sudur (Head of religious endowments, charity and judicial affairs; served as Chief Qazi / Qazi-ul-Quzat)

Provincial & Local Administration: Empire divided into Subahs (provinces, initially 12 under Akbar, increased to 15, and 21 under Aurangzeb) $\rightarrow$ Sarkars (districts) $\rightarrow$ Parganas (sub-districts / talukas) $\rightarrow$ Grama (villages); Provincial Officers: Subahdar / Sipahsalar (provincial governor in charge of law, order and defense) and Provincial Diwan (financial head independent of Subahdar, directly accountable to central imperial Diwan - dual checks on provincial power); Sarkar Officers: Faujdar (executive and military head, suppressed rebellions, maintained law and order) and Amalguzar (revenue collector); Pargana Officers: Shiqdar (law and order), Amil (revenue assessment), Qanungo (keeper of revenue records), Karkun (clerks); Village Officers: Muqaddam (village headman) and Patwari (village accountant)

Mansabdari System: Core civil-military administrative framework introduced by Akbar in 1571; 'Mansab' means rank / position; Every military and civil officer held a specific Mansab; Dual Rank Structure (introduced by Akbar in 1595): Zat Rank (personal rank determining status in imperial hierarchy and personal salary) and Sawar Rank (military rank determining exact number of horsemen/cavalry the officer was required to maintain); Rules of Sawar: Sawar rank could NEVER exceed Zat rank; Dagh System (branding of royal horses with imperial seal) and Chehra / Huliya system (descriptive descriptive rolls of soldiers to prevent fraud and ghost soldiers); Dhaspe / Du-aspa Sih-aspa System (introduced by Jahangir: Allowed selected noble to maintain double the number of cavalry without increasing his Zat rank / salary); Decreasing military efficiency under later Mughals as nobility grew faster than available revenue (Jagirdari crisis)

Jagirdari System & Types of Jagirs: System of paying salaries to Mansabdars through land revenue assignments: Naqdi (paid directly in cash from imperial treasury) vs Jagirdar (assigned right to collect land revenue from designated territory called Jagir); Types of Jagirs: 1. Tankha Jagir (regular salary assignment, transferable every 3 to 4 years to prevent local power bases), 2. Mashrut Jagir (conditional jagir given for military emergency or specific assignment), 3. Inam / Madad-i-Maash / Suyurghal Jagir (revenue-free grant given to religious scholars, saints, charities, non-transferable and hereditary), 4. Watan Jagir (hereditary, non-transferable jagir granted to autonomous indigenous rulers like Rajput chiefs in their ancestral homelands); Distinction between Khalisa land (crown land whose revenue went directly to royal imperial treasury) and Jagir land (assigned to mansabdars); Jama (estimated assessed revenue) vs Hasil (actual realized revenue); Widening gap between Jama and Hasil led to agrarian distress and alienation of peasantry

Land Revenue Administration & Dahsala System: Todar Mal's Bandobast / Ain-i-Dahsala introduced in 1580: Average production and average prices of past 10 years (1570–1580) calculated; State's share fixed at 1/3rd of average yield, payable preferably in cash (using conversion schedules / Dastur-ul-Amal); Land Measurement: Bamboo rod joined with iron rings (Tanab) replaced rope; Land Classification based on continuity of cultivation: 1. Polaj (annually cultivated, never left fallow), 2. Parauti (left fallow for 1-2 years to regain fertility), 3. Chachar (left fallow for 3-4 years), 4. Banjar (uncultivated for 5 or more years); Revenue Assessment Methods: Zabti / Dahsala (measurement-based assessment), Ghalla-Bakhshi / Batai (crop-sharing system: Bhaoli, Khet-batai, Lang-batai), Nasaq (rough estimation based on previous years' revenue)

Akbar's Religious Policy & Indo-Islamic Architecture: Religious Evolution: Early orthodox phase $\rightarrow$ Abolished Pilgrim Tax (1563) and Jizya (1564); Built Ibadat Khana (Hall of Worship at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, initially opened to Sunni theologians, opened in 1578 to all religions: Hindus, Jains like Harivijaya Suri, Parsis like Dastur Meherji Rana, Christians like Father Aquaviva); Issued Mahzar / Infallibility Decree (1579 drafted by Sheikh Mubarak, declared Akbar supreme arbiter in case of conflicting religious interpretations); Propounded Tauhid-i-Ilahi / Din-i-Ilahi (1582, ethical spiritual code based on reason, rejected idol worship, only 18 nobles accepted including Birbal); Policy of Sulh-i-Kul (universal peace and tolerance for all); Architecture: Red sandstone, trabeate and arcuate fusion, Gujarat/Bengal domes: Humayun's Tomb (Delhi, prototype of Taj Mahal, charbagh garden layout, red sandstone with white marble trim, double dome); Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza commemorating Gujarat victory, Panch Mahal 5-storeyed pillar palace, Tomb of Salim Chishti); Shah Jahan's marble zenith: Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Taj Mahal (pietra dura inlay, bulbous dome, minarets, riverfront garden)

CSAT_Grade6.keywords: Core thesis extraction, Extreme word elimination, Textual evidence matching, 20+ correct target

sub_items.text: Rule 1 - The Extreme Word Filter: Words like 'All', 'Always', 'Never', 'Only', 'Inevitably', 'Must', 'Entirely' are FALSE in UPSC RC 95% of the time

Rule 2 - The Assumption Test (The Collapse Rule): An assumption is an unstated FOUNDATION. If you negate the statement and the author's argument falls apart, it IS an assumption. If argument survives, it is NOT an assumption
Rule 3 - The Outside Knowledge Prison: Never bring personal GS knowledge into the passage. Even if an option is scientifically true in real life, if it is NOT in the passage, it is INCORRECT
Rule 4 - Inference vs Implication: Direct statement vs reading between lines; inference must be 100% logically provable from given sentences
Rule 5 - Critical Message vs Corollary: The author's primary burning objective versus a secondary side-effect
Speed Method: Read the question stem FIRST before reading the passage (know what you are hunting for)

CSAT_Grade6.topic: Percentages & Profit-Loss: The "₹100 Trick" (No Formula Required)
CSAT_Grade6.keywords: Base 100 substitution, Fraction-to-percentage mental scale (1/8=12.5%, 1/6=16.67%), Price vs Consumption inverse balance

sub_items.text: The ₹100 Magic Model: Always assume the starting unknown cost is ₹100. Never use 'Let $x$ be the cost'
Two-Step Successive Percentages: If price increases by 20% and then decreases by 10%: Start ₹100 $\rightarrow$ +₹20 = ₹120. Now 10% of 120 is ₹12. ₹120 - ₹12 = ₹108. Net change is +8% (Profit of 8%)
Profit & Loss Markup: Cost Price (CP) vs Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP); Discount is ALWAYS calculated on MP, Profit is ALWAYS calculated on CP
Equal Selling Price Trap: When two articles are sold at the same price, one at $x\%$ profit and other at $x\%$ loss, there is ALWAYS a net loss of $(x/10)^2\%$
Mental Math: 10% is moving decimal one place left. 5% is half of 10%. 1% is moving decimal two places left

CSAT_Grade6.topic: Averages: The "Physical Balance Scale" Mental Model
CSAT_Grade6.keywords: Deviations from assumed mean, Inclusion/Exclusion of teacher or member, Zero algebraic equations

sub_items.text: The Physical Balance Scale Model: An average is simply the fulcrum where weights balance out. Surplus on one side must equal deficit on the other side

The New Person Joining / Leaving Shortcut: If average age of 10 students is 15 years, and a teacher joins making the new average 16 years: Teacher brought 15 (for herself) + 1 extra year for each of the 11 people = $15 + 11 = 26$ years!
Replacement Trick: When one person is replaced by another: Weight difference = Number of people $\times$ Change in average
Weighted Average / Tug of War: When combining two groups of sizes $N_1$ and $N_2$ with averages $A_1$ and $A_2$: Average sits closer to the larger group
Cricket Bowling/Batting Averages: Batting average = Total runs / Total dismissals (NOT innings played!); Bowling average = Runs conceded / Wickets taken
Arithmetic Progression Median: For any consecutive sequence (e.g. 5, 10, 15, 20, 25), the average is simply the exact middle number (or $(First + Last) / 2$)

CSAT_Grade6.topic: Syllogisms: The "Circle Venn Diagram" Story Method
CSAT_Grade6.keywords: All A are B (Baby circle inside Mom circle), Some A are B (Overlapping circles), No A is B (Two disconnected islands)

sub_items.text: The Circle Venn Diagram Method: Draw boundaries like physical fences. Every statement is a physical container
'All A are B': Draw Circle A completely INSIDE Circle B
'Some A are B': Draw Circle A and Circle B overlapping (intersection exists)
'No A is B': Draw Circle A and Circle B completely separated with a barrier wall
The Golden Test for 'Definitely Follows': A conclusion follows ONLY if it is true in EVERY possible diagram you can draw. If you can draw even ONE valid diagram where it fails, it DOES NOT follow
Either-Or Complementary Pairs: If Conclusion 1 is 'Some A are B' and Conclusion 2 is 'No A is B', and neither is individually certain, it is an 'Either 1 or 2 follows' pair

CSAT_Grade6.topic: Direction Sense & Blood Relations: The Family Tree & Compass
CSAT_Grade6.keywords: North-South-East-West cross diagram, Pythagoras 3-4-5 triangle shortcut, Family generation levels

sub_items.text: The Compass Cross Method: Always draw the 4-direction cross: North (Up), South (Down), East (Right), West (Left)
Turning Left vs Right: If facing North, Right = East, Left = West. If facing South, Right = West, Left = East (reversed!)
Shortest Distance / Pythagoras Theorem: In a right-angled triangle, Distance = $\sqrt{Base^2 + Height^2}$ (remember common triples: 3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13)
Shadows at Sunrise vs Sunset: At Sunrise, Sun is in East $\rightarrow$ Shadow falls to the WEST. At Sunset, Sun is in West $\rightarrow$ Shadow falls to the EAST
Blood Relations - Generation Tree: Draw older generations UP and younger generations DOWN. Use '+' for Male, '-' for Female, '=' for Married couple, '-' for Siblings
Decodable Phrases: 'Father of my mother' = Maternal Grandfather; 'Son of only brother of my father' = Paternal Cousin

CSAT_Grade6.topic: Calendar & Clocks: The "7-Day Week Circle" Rule
CSAT_Grade6.keywords: Ordinary year = 1 odd day, Leap year = 2 odd days, Angle between clock hands formula visualizer

sub_items.text: The 7-Day Cycle / Odd Days Method: Any number of days divided by 7: The REMAINDER is the number of 'Odd Days'. Normal year (365 days) has 1 odd day ($365 = 52 \times 7 + 1$). Leap year (366 days) has 2 odd days
Leap Year Rule: Divisible by 4 is a leap year; century years must be divisible by 400 (1600, 2000 are leap years; 1700, 1800, 1900 are NOT leap years)
Day of Next Year: If 1st January 2023 was Sunday, 1st January 2024 is Monday (+1). But 1st January 2025 is Wednesday (+2 because 2024 was leap year with Feb 29)
Clock Angle Formula / Hands Movement: Minute hand moves 6° per minute ($360° / 60$). Hour hand moves 0.5° per minute ($30° / 60$). Relative speed = $5.5°$ per minute
Right Angles & Coinciding: Hands coincide once every hour (11 times in 12 hours, 22 times in 24 hours); Hands are at 90° twice every hour (22 times in 12 hours, 44 times in 24 hours)
Faulty Clock Catch-up: If a clock gains 5 minutes per hour, in 12 hours it gains 60 minutes (1 full hour)

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Number System: Unit Digit Cyclicity & Exponent Powers
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Ferris Wheel Loop, Cyclicity of 2, 3, 7, 8 (Cycle 4), 4 & 9 (Cycle 2), Fixed endings 0, 1, 5, 6

sub_items.text: Master the 4-step Ferris Wheel rule: divide the power by 4, the remainder is the effective power
Handle fixed digits: Any power of 0, 1, 5, 6 always ends in the exact same digit
Solve 5 unit digit questions: Find unit digit of 7^95, 3^65, (3^65 x 6^59 x 7^71)

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Number System: Remainder Theorem & Successive Division
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Successive division remainder reconstruction, Polynomial remainder theorem, Factor cancelation trick

sub_items.text: Successive Division Ladder: Work backwards from quotient 1 to reconstruct the original dividend
Factor cancelation remainder rule: If dividing product (e.g. 85 x 87... by 100), factor out 25 and 4
Negative Remainders: Use (divisor - remainder) to simplify powers near multiples (e.g. 2^31 / 9)
Solve 5 UPSC PYQs on remainder of consecutive product and successive division

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Number System: Divisibility Rules (3, 7, 9, 11, 13)
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Sum of digits (3 & 9), Alternating sum of digits (11), Triple subtraction method (7, 11, 13)

sub_items.text: Rule for 3 & 9: Sum of digits must be divisible by 3 or 9
Rule for 11: Difference between sum of odd-place digits and even-place digits must be 0 or multiple of 11
Combined Rule for 7, 11, 13: Split number into 3-digit groups from right, alternate signs; difference must divide by 7, 11, or 13
Solve 5 missing-digit problems: If 481_673 is divisible by 9, find the missing digit

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Number System: Factors, Multiples & Prime Factorization
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Total factors formula (p+1)(q+1)(r+1), Prime factorization tree, Odd vs Even factors

sub_items.text: Break any composite number into prime bases: N = 2^a x 3^b x 5^c
Total number of factors = (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1)
Number of even factors: a x (b + 1)(c + 1); Number of odd factors: (b + 1)(c + 1)
Practice finding total and prime factors for 720, 1080, and 1200

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Number System: Trailing Zeroes in Factorials
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Legendre's formula, 2x5 pair rule, Powers of 5 counting in n!

sub_items.text: Understand zero creation: A trailing zero is created ONLY by 2 x 5 = 10
In any factorial (n!), 2s are plentiful, so number of zeroes is governed entirely by count of 5s
Legendre's Formula: [n/5] + [n/25] + [n/125] + [n/625]... (integer quotients only)
Calculate trailing zeroes for 100! (24 zeroes), 200! (49 zeroes), and 500! (124 zeroes)

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Percentages: The ₹100 Bill Method & Fraction Ladder
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Base 100 substitution, Fraction ladder (1/6 = 16.66%, 1/8 = 12.5%), Price vs Consumption inverse balance

sub_items.text: Never assume 'x': Always set the original unknown quantity to ₹100
Price-Consumption Inverse Rule: If price goes UP by 1/n, consumption must drop by 1/(n+1) to keep budget constant
Solve 5 problems: Petrol price rises by 25%, sugar price drops by 20%

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Percentages: Successive Changes & Population Growth
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Formula a + b + ab/100, Compounding vs simple percentage change, Area expansion problems

sub_items.text: Net Change Formula: Net % = a + b + (ab/100) (use negative sign for discounts/reductions)
Rectangle Area Effect: Length +20%, Breadth -10% -> Net area change = +20 - 10 + (-200/100) = +8%
Two successive discounts of 10% and 20%: -10 - 20 + 200/100 = -28% (Single equivalent discount 28%)
Solve 5 UPSC successive percentage problems

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Profit and Loss: Markup, Discounts & Faulty Balances
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Cost Price (CP) vs Selling Price (SP) vs Marked Price (MP), Dishonest shopkeeper formula

sub_items.text: Distinguish bases: Profit/Loss is ALWAYS on CP; Discount is ALWAYS on Marked Price (MP)
Equal Selling Price Trap: Two items sold at same SP, one at x% profit and other at x% loss -> Always a net loss of (x/10)^2 %
Dishonest Dealer Weight Fraud: Profit % = [Error / (True Value - Error)] x 100
Solve 5 profit & loss problems with ₹100 base substitution

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Averages: The Playground Seesaw Balancing Scale
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Deviation from assumed mean, Inclusion/Exclusion of teacher, Replacement shortcut

sub_items.text: Average as Seesaw Fulcrum: Total surplus above mean must exactly balance total deficit below mean
Newcomer Joins Shortcut: Extra brought = (New Total Count) x (Increase in Average)
Replacement Formula: New person weight = Old person weight + (Count x Change in Average)
Solve 5 average age and cricket score problems mentally without multiplying large numbers

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Ratio and Proportion, Mixtures & Alligation
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: The Cross Alligation Diagram, Repeated replacement formula, Mean proportional

sub_items.text: The Alligation Cross: (Cheaper Price) (Dearer Price) -> Mean Price in center -> Cross-subtract to get quantity ratio
Repeated Replacement Formula: Final Pure Liquid = Initial Liquid x (1 - x / V)^n
Ratio scaling trick: To combine A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, multiply to make B equal (8:12:15)
Solve 5 mixture and milk-water replacement problems

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Time and Work: The LCM Total-Units Method
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Total cookies LCM method, Efficiency rates, Alternate day work cycles

sub_items.text: Step 1: Set Total Work = LCM of given days (Never use 1/12 + 1/18 fractions!)
Step 2: Find daily cookie baking rate (Efficiency = Total Work / Days)
Alternate Day Cycle: Sum work done in a 2-day cycle, find completed cycles, divide remaining cookies
Solve 5 work problems: A in 10 days, B in 15 days, working together vs alternate days

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Pipes and Cisterns: Inlets vs Outlets
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Inlet positive work (+), Leak/Outlet negative work (-), Capacity LCM method

sub_items.text: Total Tank Capacity = LCM of filling and emptying times
Inlet pipe is (+) rate units/hour; Leak / waste pipe is (-) rate units/hour
Net rate = (Inlet rate) - (Leak rate); Time to fill = Total Capacity / Net rate
Solve 5 tank filling problems with simultaneous leaks

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Time, Speed & Distance: 5/18 Converter & Harmonic Average Speed
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: km/h to m/s conversion x 5/18, Average speed 2xy/(x+y), Relative speed same vs opposite

sub_items.text: The Unit Converter: km/h -> m/s multiply by 5/18. Multiples: 18km/h=5m/s, 36=10, 54=15, 72=20, 90=25
Average Speed for equal distance trips = 2xy / (x + y) (Harmonic mean, never arithmetic mean!)
Relative Speed: Moving towards each other = S1 + S2; Moving in same direction = S1 - S2
Solve 5 speed-time-distance problems with unit conversions

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Trains: Crossing Poles vs Platforms & Relative Speed
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Crossing pole (Distance = Train length), Crossing platform (Distance = Train + Platform), Parallel tracks

sub_items.text: Crossing Pole / Man / Tree: Distance covered = Length of Train only (pole width is zero)
Crossing Platform / Bridge / Tunnel: Distance covered = Train Length + Platform Length
Two Trains Crossing Each Other: Distance = Train1 + Train2; Speed = S1 + S2 (Opposite) or S1 - S2 (Same)
Solve 5 train crossing problems under 60 seconds each

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Boats and Streams: Upstream vs Downstream
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Downstream speed (u + v), Upstream speed (u - v), Still water speed (D + U)/2

sub_items.text: Downstream Speed D = u + v (Stream aids the boat)
Upstream Speed U = u - v (Stream opposes the boat)
Speed of Boat in still water u = (D + U) / 2; Speed of Stream v = (D - U) / 2
Solve 5 boat round-trip and stream rate problems

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Permutations & Combinations: Handshake Theorem & Tie/Gap Tricks
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Fundamental counting principle, Handshakes n(n-1)/2, Tie method (keep together), Gap method (never together)

sub_items.text: Permutation = Arranging in line (order matters); Combination = Selecting team (order irrelevant)
Handshake Theorem: n people shaking hands once = n(n - 1) / 2
Tie Method (Must be together): Pack items in 1 bag, arrange external items, multiply by internal permutations
Gap Method (Never together): Place unrestricted items first, place restricted items in the gaps
Solve 5 arrangements of boys & girls and committee selections

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Probability: Basic Events, Dice, Coins & Independent Odds
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: P(E) = Favorable / Total, Independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B), Complementary P(not E) = 1 - P(E)

sub_items.text: Basic Probability = Number of Favorable Outcomes / Total Sample Space
At Least One Event: P(At least one) = 1 - P(None happen)
Independent Events: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
Solve 5 probability problems: 2 dice sum of 7, coin toss sequences, card draws

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Clocks: Angle Formula & Overlap Points
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Angle formula |30H - 5.5M|, 11 overlaps in 12 hours, 22 right angles in 12 hours

sub_items.text: Universal Angle Formula: Angle = |30H - (11/2)M| degrees
Relative Speed of Hands: Minute hand 6 deg/min, Hour hand 0.5 deg/min -> Relative speed 5.5 deg/min
Coinciding Hands: Overlap happens every 65 5/11 minutes (11 times in 12 hours, 22 times in 24 hours)
Calculate angle at 3:40, 7:20, 8:30, and find when hands overlap between 4 and 5

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Calendar: The 7-Day Cycle & Odd Days Calculation
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: 7-day loop remainder, Ordinary year = 1 odd day, Leap year = 2 odd days, Century odd days

sub_items.text: Odd Days = Remainder after dividing total days by 7
Year shift: Ordinary year shifts day by +1; Leap year (has Feb 29) shifts day by +2
Century Odd Days: 100 years = 5 odd days; 200 years = 3; 300 years = 1; 400 years = 0
Calculate day of the week for any historical or future date

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Cubes and Dice: Opposite Faces & Cut Painted Cubes
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Standard vs General dice, Unfolded cross dice opposite faces, Painted cube cutting formulas

sub_items.text: Unfolded Dice Rule: Alternate faces in the same row/column are opposite to each other (skip 1 square)
Painted Cube Cut into n x n x n small cubes: Corner cubes (3 painted) = 8 always
Middle edge cubes (2 painted) = 12(n - 2); Face center cubes (1 painted) = 6(n - 2)^2; Inner core (0 painted) = (n - 2)^3
Solve 5 unfolded dice and painted cube problems

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Blood Relations: Generation Family Tree Mapping
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Generation level vertical mapping, Gender symbols (+ for male, - for female), Marriage '=' sign

sub_items.text: Draw generations vertically: Grandparents on top, Parents middle, Children below
Use crisp symbols: (+) for Male, (-) for Female, (=) for Husband-Wife, (---) for Siblings
Break down long statements backwards: 'He is the son of the only daughter of my mother'
Solve 5 complex family relation deduction puzzles

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Direction Sense: 8-Point Compass & Pythagoras Trajectory
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: 8-point compass, Pythagoras distance sqrt(a^2 + b^2), Left/Right turns facing South

sub_items.text: The 8-point compass: North, South, East, West, NE, NW, SE, SW
Inverted turns: When walking South, turning RIGHT moves towards West; turning LEFT moves towards East
Shortest Distance = Pythagoras formula sqrt(x^2 + y^2) (Look for 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 triangles)
Solve 5 multi-turn walking trajectory problems

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Syllogisms: Mom & Baby Venn Circles & Either-Or Rules
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: All A are B (inner circle), Some A are B (overlap), No A is B (disjoint), Complementary pairs

sub_items.text: 'All A are B': Draw Circle A completely inside Circle B. Anything in A is in B
'Some A are B': Draw overlapping circles with shared slice
The Golden Test: A conclusion follows ONLY if it holds in EVERY single valid diagram you can draw
Complementary Pair (Either-Or): When conclusions are 'Some A are B' and 'No A is B', neither certain alone
Solve 5 syllogism questions with 3 statements and 3 conclusions

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Seating Arrangements & Complex Puzzles
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: Linear row facing North/South, Circular table facing center vs facing out, Cross-grid matrix

sub_items.text: Linear Row: Facing North -> your right is their right; Facing South -> directions reversed
Circular Table facing center: Clockwise is Left, Anti-clockwise is Right
Grid Matrix: Plot definite clues first (X is lawyer living on floor 3), never assume possibilities early
Solve 5 linear and circular seating arrangement puzzles

CSAT_MicroTopics.topic: Reading Comprehension: The 4-Step 'Sherlocking' Method
CSAT_MicroTopics.keywords: 50+ Marks RC, Question First, Sentence Anchor, Murder Extreme Words, Modest Claim Selection

sub_items.text: Step 1: Read Question Stem FIRST — Identify if hunting for 'Critical Assumption', 'Corollary', or 'Crux'
Step 2: Scan passage for the exact sentence anchor containing question keywords
Step 3: Murder Extreme Words — Eliminate options containing 'always', 'never', 'solely', 'only', 'banned', 'entirely'
Step 4: Pick Modest Claim — Correct answers use cautious phrasing ('may', 'can', 'contributes to')
Practice 5 UPSC official passages using the 4-step Sherlocking method
